CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.ENGINEERING_CLAIM: A parser used to accept a language must identify the language/version, lexical rules and disambiguation policy it implements, and distinguish recognition from structure and interpretation.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.CLAIM_CLASS: Conditional engineering property derived from formal mechanisms and their boundaries
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.BEARER_OR_SUBJECT: A versioned grammar/lexer/parser configuration and finite input byte sequence.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.FAILURE_MODE_OR_LIMIT_ADDRESSED: Undocumented priority, lexer/parser disagreement, silently ignored suffixes, or treating deterministic syntax as settled stakeholder meaning.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MECHANISM: Fix decoding, tokenization, start rule, end-of-input convention and ambiguity policy; check that parsing accepts exactly under that contract and reports the selected structure or alternatives.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Retain an explicit accepted-language contract; choose LL/LR/GLR/PEG/scannerless mechanisms according to grammar and consumer, with error policy recorded.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.EXPECTED_PAYOFF: Reproducible language admission and a clear place to diagnose grammar/implementation disagreements.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.PAYOFF_EVIDENCE_NOT_JUST_RATIONALE: Mechanistic/formal support: Language-definition and algorithm properties apply to the chosen grammar formalism; grammar equivalence or implementation correctness is not established for an arbitrary parser. No direct comparative engineering-payoff experiment for this whole reconstructed property is established.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Text has a language whose grouping or token boundaries affect a downstream execution, analysis or authoring decision.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.ALTERNATIVE_MECHANISMS: Use an established structured format and its existing parser when a record schema suffices; a two-field data entry form does not need a custom grammar.

APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Text has a language whose grouping or token boundaries affect a downstream execution, analysis or authoring decision.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Known non-trigger: The examined input is not being admitted syntactically and is not supplied to any parse-structure consumer. For example, a consumer receives an already established scalar value and makes no parsing/admission claim. Lower-cost option already recorded: Use an established structured format and its existing parser when a record schema suffices; a two-field data entry form does not need a custom grammar. Applicability and evidence limit: An existing structured-format parser or a small form validator remains applicable when it performs syntactic admission. It can establish P cheaply if its evidence covers full consumption, errors and the declared ambiguity policy; choosing an existing parser does not make A false.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ASSUMPTIONS_AND_PRECONDITIONS: The intended syntactic language and its policy are specified; decoder and lexer are part of the boundary; semantic actions do not secretly change the recognizer contract.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ENVIRONMENT_AND_BOUNDARY: Covers syntactic admission. Binding, typing, executable authorization and natural-language intent are separate.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.SCOPE_AND_EXCLUSIONS: Language-definition and algorithm properties apply to the chosen grammar formalism; grammar equivalence or implementation correctness is not established for an arbitrary parser.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.AUTHORITY_OR_NORMATIVE_BASIS_IF_APPLICAB: Source language definitions/theorems or tool contracts are authoritative only within their versioned scope. This reconstructed research property is not a normative requirement for any target.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.INPUT_AND_EVIDENCE_PROVENANCE_REQUIREMEN: Record exact input/model, language/tool version, dependencies, evaluator, observation method and source locators; separate constructed examples, source proofs and observed tool outcomes. Grammar version, lexical decoding, parse-action side effects, or consumption status unavailable; a timeout is UNKNOWN, not rejection.

DEPENDENCIES_AND_CONFLICTS.NOTE: Choosing one parse can hide rather than resolve ambiguity; generalized and deterministic algorithms have materially different costs and recognized languages. Relations collection provides directional shared-bearer conditions.

APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.FAILURE_OF_ASSUMPTIONS: Undocumented priority, lexer/parser disagreement, silently ignored suffixes, or treating deterministic syntax as settled stakeholder meaning. A missing premise produces UNKNOWN for the guarantee, not a fabricated PASS.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.COST_AND_MAINTENANCE_BURDEN: Grammar maintenance, ambiguity diagnostics, parser-table/packrat memory, lexical-version compatibility and corpus regression costs.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.RETIREMENT_OR_REENTRY_CONDITION: Re-enter on Change to encoding, lexical rules, precedence, choice order, grammar, parser algorithm/version or semantic-action admission policy. Retire this mechanism when Use an established structured format and its existing parser when a record schema suffices; a two-field data entry form does not need a custom grammar.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: Explicit grammar, lexical contract and ambiguity policy: A parser used to accept a language must identify the language/version, lexical rules and disambiguation policy it implements, and distinguish recognition from structure and interpretation.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: For every admitted instance/transition explicitly covered by the stated rule and applicability guard; a worked example is not evidence for all programs. Covers syntactic admission. Binding, typing, executable authorization and natural-language intent are separate.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: A versioned grammar/lexer/parser configuration and finite input byte sequence.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Evaluate against the recorded version/environment; execution/transition statements range over the rule's modeled executions, while current evidence is a dated observation. For configured G and decoder D: strict_accept(x) iff D succeeds, the start parse consumes the entire required input, no unreconciled syntax errors remain, and the resulting alternative set/selection obeys the declared ambiguity policy. This is not a semantic-validity predicate.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ASSUMPTIONS: The intended syntactic language and its policy are specified; decoder and lexer are part of the boundary; semantic actions do not secretly change the recognizer contract.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: A(x): x is an input for a syntactic admission or parse-structure consumer.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: For configured G and decoder D: strict_accept(x) iff D succeeds, the start parse consumes the entire required input, no unreconciled syntax errors remain, and the resulting alternative set/selection obeys the declared ambiguity policy. This is not a semantic-validity predicate.

SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.NOTE: This operational rule is a synthesis for intake evaluation, not a formula quoted from a source theorem; source theorems remain bounded by their own language and hypotheses.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Read versioned language report and effective parser configuration; Instrument parser on the exact byte input. Map these values into the rule without substituting a successful tool exit for semantic truth.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: The intended syntactic language and its policy are specified; decoder and lexer are part of the boundary; semantic actions do not secretly change the recognizer contract. Required witness data: grammar_contract and admission_trace.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: Run the specified parser and examine consumption/error/ambiguity outputs; compare to independent examples or grammar derivations. Exact language equivalence needs a restricted proof and is generally not decided by a test corpus.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: The finite instance/trace checks described by the evaluator may be executable. Quantification over all programs, contexts or executions requires the source's restricted theorem/proof; finite testing is incomplete, and timeout yields UNKNOWN.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.POSITIVE_WITNESS: Constructed: the grammar E := E - N | N with declared left associativity parses 1-2-3 as (1-2)-3, consuming all input.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: Constructed: accepting the prefix 1 from 1 garbage under a whole-input contract fails; choosing (1-2)-3 does not establish that a stakeholder intended that arithmetic.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: Grammar version, lexical decoding, parse-action side effects, or consumption status unavailable; a timeout is UNKNOWN, not rejection. Missing evidence is not evidence that the guard is false. If A is already known true, an unestablished model, premise, proof or coverage leaves the operational judgment UNKNOWN through P/E; if a fact needed to decide A itself is unknown, report A=UNKNOWN. Only an established false A permits INAPPLICABLE.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: The examined input is not being admitted syntactically and is not supplied to any parse-structure consumer. For example, a consumer receives an already established scalar value and makes no parsing/admission claim.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False positive: treating an incomplete boundary/proxy as the whole claim (Undocumented priority, lexer/parser disagreement, silently ignored suffixes, or treating deterministic syntax as settled stakeholder meaning.). False negative: rejecting a valid instance because a conservative analysis or restricted proof language cannot express it; distinguish analyzer rejection from demonstrated semantic failure.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: A checker that rejects everything, empty accepted corpus, erased error nodes, or an observation model that omits the disputed behavior can make apparent success vacuous. Choosing one parse can hide rather than resolve ambiguity; generalized and deterministic algorithms have materially different costs and recognized languages.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Change to encoding, lexical rules, precedence, choice order, grammar, parser algorithm/version or semantic-action admission policy.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Grammar maintenance, ambiguity diagnostics, parser-table/packrat memory, lexical-version compatibility and corpus regression costs. Cheaper path: Use an established structured format and its existing parser when a record schema suffices; a two-field data entry form does not need a custom grammar. Applicability and evidence limit: An existing structured-format parser or a small form validator remains applicable when it performs syntactic admission. It can establish P cheaply if its evidence covers full consumption, errors and the declared ambiguity policy; choosing an existing parser does not make A false.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Foundational definitions and algorithm/tool contracts support the distinction; no evidence establishes a universally best parser or automatic recovery of intended meaning.

FORMALISATION_PROVENANCE.LIMIT: The intake predicate is not represented as a published universal theorem.

APPLICABILITY_A.TRUE: A(x): x is an input for a syntactic admission or parse-structure consumer.
APPLICABILITY_A.FALSE: The examined input is not being admitted syntactically and is not supplied to any parse-structure consumer. For example, a consumer receives an already established scalar value and makes no parsing/admission claim.
APPLICABILITY_A.UNKNOWN: The truth of the applicability guard itself is not established. When the guard is known true, missing model/premise/proof/coverage evidence belongs to unresolved P/E and yields overall UNKNOWN, not A=false. Specific evidence gaps: Grammar version, lexical decoding, parse-action side effects, or consumption status unavailable; a timeout is UNKNOWN, not rejection.

PROPERTY_P.TRUE: The precise rule holds for the stated model/instance and quantified scope.
PROPERTY_P.FALSE: A counterexample within the guard violates the rule.
PROPERTY_P.UNDETERMINED: Truth is not settled by available observation or proof; it is not inferred from missing evidence.

OPERATIONAL_EVALUATION.CURRENT_EVALUATION: Schema and constructed witnesses only; no target instance was evaluated.

EVALUATOR_OUTCOMES.PASS: Adequate, current evidence establishes P for the declared scope and A is true.
EVALUATOR_OUTCOMES.FAIL: Adequate counterevidence establishes a violation with A true.
EVALUATOR_OUTCOMES.UNKNOWN: A or P is unresolved, evidence stale, solver times out or scope is incomplete.
EVALUATOR_OUTCOMES.INAPPLICABLE: The examined input is not being admitted syntactically and is not supplied to any parse-structure consumer. For example, a consumer receives an already established scalar value and makes no parsing/admission claim.

EVIDENCE_SUFFICIENCY_E.SIGNATURE: E_p(evidence, target={the named predicate=true or the named predicate=false}, scope) -> adequacy judgment
EVIDENCE_SUFFICIENCY_E.SUFFICIENT: The evidence, its provenance, coverage and evaluator soundness conditions justify that specifically named truth/falsity verdict in the declared scope.
EVIDENCE_SUFFICIENCY_E.INSUFFICIENT_OR_UNKNOWN: The required premise, observation, source/implementation bridge or evaluator coverage is missing or unresolved. This does not decide predicate truth.
EVIDENCE_SUFFICIENCY_E.NEGATIVE_WITNESS_RULE: A valid counterexample to the actual predicate can establish predicate=false with adequate evidence and overall evaluator FAIL. Evidence refuting only a stronger overclaim does not establish the retained predicate=false.
EVIDENCE_SUFFICIENCY_E.LIMIT: Adequacy for one target/scope does not establish a different predicate, unrestricted truth or the original candidate if the named predicate instead tests its critique.

FORMAL_OR_THEORETICAL_RESULT.LIMITS: Language-definition and algorithm properties apply to the chosen grammar formalism; grammar equivalence or implementation correctness is not established for an arbitrary parser.

REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.CLAIM: No independent replication establishing this whole engineering property was found in the bounded lane search.

INDUSTRIAL_OR_FIELD_CASE.CLAIM: Official tool/language material demonstrates an implemented concern; published research models inform production languages.

NEGATIVE_RESULT_OR_INCIDENT.CLAIM: Choosing one parse can hide rather than resolve ambiguity; generalized and deterministic algorithms have materially different costs and recognized languages.
NEGATIVE_RESULT_OR_INCIDENT.LIMITS: Distinguish a formal counterexample, documented limitation and measured slowdown from a deployed security incident; this lane does not invent incidents.

STANDARD_OR_NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT.CLAIM: Language reports and official API contracts define behavior within their own versioned scope.

EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.NEXT_DISCRIMINATOR: Run the specified parser and examine consumption/error/ambiguity outputs; compare to independent examples or grammar derivations. Exact language equivalence needs a restricted proof and is generally not decided by a test corpus. Supply missing grammar_contract / admission_trace evidence before strengthening the verdict.

RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: The generic negative-case verdict conflates failure of the retained predicate with failure of a stronger implication. XA10 gives a well-typed, safe function returning zero that violates an intended increment requirement; C0010-P01 deliberately claims only avoidance of Bad_L. XA12 gives a function satisfying its encoded postcondition result=0 but not the intended increment; C0012-P01 is the relative formal-specification claim. In both cases the retained predicate can remain true, yet EXPECTED_A_P_E.NEGATIVE assigns A=true, P=false and E=FAIL. The phrase for the precise violated rule/overclaim does not identify a separate overclaim predicate and leaves the case evaluator capable of falsely failing the retained property. Analogous ambiguity occurs where unauthorized effects, uncalibrated physical time or out-of-fragment seq refute only additional inferences.

Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

REVIEW_FINDINGS_AND_DISPOSITION.LIMIT: No listed finding is not a guarantee of correctness; reviewers and their sampled documentary checks are described in the validation report.

INTAKE.CROSSWALK_ELIGIBILITY_WITH_REASON: Eligible as a conditional candidate with explicit evidence ceiling; rejected/ceremonial records are retained as failure boundaries rather than favorable recommendations.

Which observation/evaluator could establish the rule, and which missing premise yields UNKNOWN?
What demonstrates grammar_contract and admission_trace rather than a label or empty accepted corpus?
Would the stated cheaper path achieve the actual consumer objective?
PROHIBITED_OVERCLAIMS: Language-definition and algorithm properties apply to the chosen grammar formalism; grammar equivalence or implementation correctness is not established for an arbitrary parser.
No claim that a proof, parser, graph, type, capability label or static check establishes natural-language intention without a separate validated bridge.

If A is already known true, an unestablished model, premise, proof or coverage leaves the operational judgment UNKNOWN through P/E; if a fact needed to decide A itself is unknown, report A=UNKNOWN. Only an established false A permits INAPPLICABLE.

False negative: rejecting a valid instance because a conservative analysis or restricted proof language cannot express it; distinguish analyzer rejection from demonstrated semantic failure.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: A checker that rejects everything, empty accepted corpus, erased error nodes, or an observation model that omits the disputed behavior can make apparent success vacuous. A minimal edit repair need not match author intent; recovery quality metrics often measure a proxy rather than successful human correction.

If a recovered or reused structure is still consumed, cheap revalidation can discharge the applicable obligation; small file size alone does not remove it.

RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: The generic negative-case verdict conflates failure of the retained predicate with failure of a stronger implication. XA10 gives a well-typed, safe function returning zero that violates an intended increment requirement; C0010-P01 deliberately claims only avoidance of Bad_L. XA12 gives a function satisfying its encoded postcondition result=0 but not the intended increment; C0012-P01 is the relative formal-specification claim. In both cases the retained predicate can remain true, yet EXPECTED_A_P_E.NEGATIVE assigns A=true, P=false and E=FAIL. The phrase for the precise violated rule/overclaim does not identify a separate overclaim predicate and leaves the case evaluator capable of falsely failing the retained property. Analogous ambiguity occurs where unauthorized effects, uncalibrated physical time or out-of-fragment seq refute only additional inferences.

Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

REVIEW_FINDINGS_AND_DISPOSITION.LIMIT: No listed finding is not a guarantee of correctness; reviewers and their sampled documentary checks are described in the validation report.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: Choose representations by consumer and preserved invariants: A representation is adequate only relative to a named consumer and explicit invariants, preserved information, reference identity and deliberate losses.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: For every admitted instance/transition explicitly covered by the stated rule and applicability guard; a worked example is not evidence for all programs. Structural validation covers representation invariants. It does not settle semantic adequacy or external domain truth.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: A representation R, source/model M, interpretation map I and downstream operation U.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Evaluate against the recorded version/environment; execution/transition statements range over the rule's modeled executions, while current evidence is a dated observation. adequate(R,M,U) requires all invariants required by U, a defined interpretation I(R), and preservation of every distinction in U.observations; deliberate losses must be observationally irrelevant to U. Unknown interpretation yields UNKNOWN, not PASS from schema validity.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ASSUMPTIONS: The consumer states what distinctions matter; references and cycles have explicit identity conventions; representation-to-subject map is inspectable.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: A(R): a consumer relies on distinctions encoded or omitted by R.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: adequate(R,M,U) requires all invariants required by U, a defined interpretation I(R), and preservation of every distinction in U.observations; deliberate losses must be observationally irrelevant to U. Unknown interpretation yields UNKNOWN, not PASS from schema validity.

SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.NOTE: This operational rule is a synthesis for intake evaluation, not a formula quoted from a source theorem; source theorems remain bounded by their own language and hypotheses.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Inspect schema, graph construction and consumer requirements; Validate target references and transformation maps; identify intended observations. Map these values into the rule without substituting a successful tool exit for semantic truth.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: The consumer states what distinctions matter; references and cycles have explicit identity conventions; representation-to-subject map is inspectable. Required witness data: representation_contract and interpretation_and_reference_map.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: Check graph/tree invariants and reference targets, then prove or test the relevant interpretation correspondence; sharing-sensitive operations require identity-aware reasoning.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: The finite instance/trace checks described by the evaluator may be executable. Quantification over all programs, contexts or executions requires the source's restricted theorem/proof; finite testing is incomplete, and timeout yields UNKNOWN.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.POSITIVE_WITNESS: Constructed: an AST supports expression evaluation while a separate binding map resolves Var nodes; a CST is retained for comment-preserving edits.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: Constructed: copying one shared mutable cell into two equal-looking tree nodes changes aliasing, so a tree-unfolding equality is insufficient for that consumer.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: Consumer observations or interpretation missing; dangling references or unavailable construction evidence cannot be assumed harmless. Missing evidence is not evidence that the guard is false. If A is already known true, an unestablished model, premise, proof or coverage leaves the operational judgment UNKNOWN through P/E; if a fact needed to decide A itself is unknown, report A=UNKNOWN. Only an established false A permits INAPPLICABLE.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: No consumer relies on any distinction encoded or omitted by the assessed representation, and no representation-adequacy claim is made for that consumer.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False positive: treating an incomplete boundary/proxy as the whole claim (Calling every graph an AST, duplicating shared/cyclic nodes, losing binding/control/provenance, or assuming a well-formed node schema establishes meaning.). False negative: rejecting a valid instance because a conservative analysis or restricted proof language cannot express it; distinguish analyzer rejection from demonstrated semantic failure.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: A checker that rejects everything, empty accepted corpus, erased error nodes, or an observation model that omits the disputed behavior can make apparent success vacuous. A universal rich graph creates complexity without a consumer; an exact dependency representation may be harder to reconstruct into executable control flow.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Node schema, equality, binding or reference conventions, source lowering, graph construction, or consumer observation changes.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Multiple representations, conversion/source maps, graph identity, cycles, analyses and synchronization across versions. Cheaper path: An immutable expression tree with no sharing-sensitive semantics can use an ordinary tagged tree; a static lookup table may need no graph. Applicability and evidence limit: A tagged tree or static table can satisfy the applicable consumer invariants without a graph or multiple IRs. Its simplicity is not evidence that no consumer relies on it; check the exact representation and observation obligations.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Concrete representation mechanisms and paper-specific correctness/optimization arguments; no proof one representation dominates all uses.

FORMALISATION_PROVENANCE.LIMIT: The intake predicate is not represented as a published universal theorem.

APPLICABILITY_A.TRUE: A(R): a consumer relies on distinctions encoded or omitted by R.
APPLICABILITY_A.FALSE: No consumer relies on any distinction encoded or omitted by the assessed representation, and no representation-adequacy claim is made for that consumer.
APPLICABILITY_A.UNKNOWN: The truth of the applicability guard itself is not established. When the guard is known true, missing model/premise/proof/coverage evidence belongs to unresolved P/E and yields overall UNKNOWN, not A=false. Specific evidence gaps: Consumer observations or interpretation missing; dangling references or unavailable construction evidence cannot be assumed harmless.

PROPERTY_P.TRUE: The precise rule holds for the stated model/instance and quantified scope.
PROPERTY_P.FALSE: A counterexample within the guard violates the rule.
PROPERTY_P.UNDETERMINED: Truth is not settled by available observation or proof; it is not inferred from missing evidence.

OPERATIONAL_EVALUATION.CURRENT_EVALUATION: Schema and constructed witnesses only; no target instance was evaluated.

EVALUATOR_OUTCOMES.PASS: Adequate, current evidence establishes P for the declared scope and A is true.
EVALUATOR_OUTCOMES.FAIL: Adequate counterevidence establishes a violation with A true.
EVALUATOR_OUTCOMES.UNKNOWN: A or P is unresolved, evidence stale, solver times out or scope is incomplete.
EVALUATOR_OUTCOMES.INAPPLICABLE: No consumer relies on any distinction encoded or omitted by the assessed representation, and no representation-adequacy claim is made for that consumer.

RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: The generic negative-case verdict conflates failure of the retained predicate with failure of a stronger implication. XA10 gives a well-typed, safe function returning zero that violates an intended increment requirement; C0010-P01 deliberately claims only avoidance of Bad_L. XA12 gives a function satisfying its encoded postcondition result=0 but not the intended increment; C0012-P01 is the relative formal-specification claim. In both cases the retained predicate can remain true, yet EXPECTED_A_P_E.NEGATIVE assigns A=true, P=false and E=FAIL. The phrase for the precise violated rule/overclaim does not identify a separate overclaim predicate and leaves the case evaluator capable of falsely failing the retained property. Analogous ambiguity occurs where unauthorized effects, uncalibrated physical time or out-of-fragment seq refute only additional inferences.

Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: Source round-trip fidelity for editing and provenance consumers: When exact source preservation is a consumer requirement, parsing/printing must retain the promised bytes or a precisely weaker normalization relation.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: For every admitted instance/transition explicitly covered by the stated rule and applicability guard; a worked example is not evidence for all programs. Byte equality implies identity of the same bytes, not correctness of external meaning; source maps are separate from semantic preservation.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Evaluate against the recorded version/environment; execution/transition statements range over the rule's modeled executions, while current evidence is a dated observation. For declared relation ≡S, print(parse(x)) ≡S x. For byte fidelity ≡S is byte equality; for normalization it is the published normalization equivalence. Neither substitutes for observational equivalence of execution.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ASSUMPTIONS: The required equality relation is declared: bytes, decoded characters, token stream or normalized syntax; encoding and line ending conventions available.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: A(x): exact or normalized source recovery is explicitly required by the consumer.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: For declared relation ≡S, print(parse(x)) ≡S x. For byte fidelity ≡S is byte equality; for normalization it is the published normalization equivalence. Neither substitutes for observational equivalence of execution.

SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.NOTE: This operational rule is a synthesis for intake evaluation, not a formula quoted from a source theorem; source theorems remain bounded by their own language and hypotheses.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Read consumer contract; do not infer from pretty printer name; Run declared parser/printer pair and compute a relation-aware difference. Map these values into the rule without substituting a successful tool exit for semantic truth.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: The required equality relation is declared: bytes, decoded characters, token stream or normalized syntax; encoding and line ending conventions available. Required witness data: source_equality_relation and round_trip_difference.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: Execute parse/print and compare under the declared equality; retain the original input as the reference. Tests quantify only over tested inputs unless a general law is proved.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: The finite instance/trace checks described by the evaluator may be executable. Quantification over all programs, contexts or executions requires the source's restricted theorem/proof; finite testing is incomplete, and timeout yields UNKNOWN.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.POSITIVE_WITNESS: Constructed: printing a full-fidelity tree reproduces the input including a trailing comment and original line endings under a byte-level contract.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: Constructed: parse to Add(1,2), then print 1+2, loses a source comment even if numeric evaluation agrees.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: Original bytes or encoding metadata unavailable, or equality contract is unspecified. Missing evidence is not evidence that the guard is false. If A is already known true, an unestablished model, premise, proof or coverage leaves the operational judgment UNKNOWN through P/E; if a fact needed to decide A itself is unknown, report A=UNKNOWN. Only an established false A permits INAPPLICABLE.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: The consumer requires neither exact source recovery nor recovery up to a declared normalization; for example, the artifact is used only for execution and no round-trip claim is made.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False positive: treating an incomplete boundary/proxy as the whole claim (An abstract tree prints equivalent-looking code but drops comments, changes layout or cannot reconstruct original bytes.). False negative: rejecting a valid instance because a conservative analysis or restricted proof language cannot express it; distinguish analyzer rejection from demonstrated semantic failure.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: A checker that rejects everything, empty accepted corpus, erased error nodes, or an observation model that omits the disputed behavior can make apparent success vacuous. RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: The generic negative-case verdict conflates failure of the retained predicate with failure of a stronger implication. XA10 gives a well-typed, safe function returning zero that violates an intended increment requirement; C0010-P01 deliberately claims only avoidance of Bad_L. XA12 gives a function satisfying its encoded postcondition result=0 but not the intended increment; C0012-P01 is the relative formal-specification claim. In both cases the retained predicate can remain true, yet EXPECTED_A_P_E.NEGATIVE assigns A=true, P=false and E=FAIL. The phrase for the precise violated rule/overclaim does not identify a separate overclaim predicate and leaves the case evaluator capable of falsely failing the retained property. Analogous ambiguity occurs where unauthorized effects, uncalibrated physical time or out-of-fragment seq refute only additional inferences.

Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: The finite instance/trace checks described by the evaluator may be executable. Quantification over all programs, contexts or executions requires the source's restricted theorem/proof; finite testing is incomplete, and timeout yields UNKNOWN.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.POSITIVE_WITNESS: A valid refutation witness: Constructed: identical Var(x) evaluates to 1 under x↦1 and 2 under x↦2; identical serialized syntax cannot identify these environments.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: Different syntax with different observations is not a valid witness against an implication whose antecedent requires structural equality; undefined observations also cannot establish inequality.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: If either term lacks a defined interpretation, semantic comparison is UNKNOWN rather than a syntactic pass. Missing evidence is not evidence that the guard is false. If A is already known true, an unestablished model, premise, proof or coverage leaves the operational judgment UNKNOWN through P/E; if a fact needed to decide A itself is unknown, report A=UNKNOWN. Only an established false A permits INAPPLICABLE.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: No structural-identity result is promoted to a semantic certificate; for example, equality is used only for identity/deduplication, with behavioral claims justified separately.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False positive: treating an incomplete boundary/proxy as the whole claim (Equal syntax resolves different names after imports; different syntax is alpha-equivalent; behavior changes when effects or evaluation policy changes.). False negative: rejecting a valid instance because a conservative analysis or restricted proof language cannot express it; distinguish analyzer rejection from demonstrated semantic failure.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: A checker that rejects everything, empty accepted corpus, erased error nodes, or an observation model that omits the disputed behavior can make apparent success vacuous. Syntax identity is not observational equivalence across contexts and says nothing about an external intention.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Any environment, binding, semantic or consumer change can invalidate a semantic claim while a tree hash remains unchanged.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: False assurance is the principal cost; proper dependency-aware caching still has modest bookkeeping cost. Cheaper path: Use the identity relation only for its declared cache/deduplication purpose and separately check relevant semantic dependencies. Applicability and evidence limit: Identity-only cache or deduplication use is a different target. If the original semantic promotion is advanced, a cheap valid counterexample can satisfy this record’s refutation-witness predicate; it does not satisfy the rejected universal candidate.

RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: The evidence partition machine values positively label the rejected candidate proposition as SUPPORTED, although the same partition limits and the retention status reject it. The evidence target is not separated from the original candidate.

The generic negative-case verdict conflates failure of the retained predicate with failure of a stronger implication. XA10 gives a well-typed, safe function returning zero that violates an intended increment requirement; C0010-P01 deliberately claims only avoidance of Bad_L. XA12 gives a function satisfying its encoded postcondition result=0 but not the intended increment; C0012-P01 is the relative formal-specification claim. In both cases the retained predicate can remain true, yet EXPECTED_A_P_E.NEGATIVE assigns A=true, P=false and E=FAIL. The phrase for the precise violated rule/overclaim does not identify a separate overclaim predicate and leaves the case evaluator capable of falsely failing the retained property. Analogous ambiguity occurs where unauthorized effects, uncalibrated physical time or out-of-fragment seq refute only additional inferences.

Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: The generic negative-case verdict conflates failure of the retained predicate with failure of a stronger implication. XA10 gives a well-typed, safe function returning zero that violates an intended increment requirement; C0010-P01 deliberately claims only avoidance of Bad_L. XA12 gives a function satisfying its encoded postcondition result=0 but not the intended increment; C0012-P01 is the relative formal-specification claim. In both cases the retained predicate can remain true, yet EXPECTED_A_P_E.NEGATIVE assigns A=true, P=false and E=FAIL. The phrase for the precise violated rule/overclaim does not identify a separate overclaim predicate and leaves the case evaluator capable of falsely failing the retained property. Analogous ambiguity occurs where unauthorized effects, uncalibrated physical time or out-of-fragment seq refute only additional inferences.

Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.ENGINEERING_CLAIM: A reference is established by current language-specific resolution in its relevant dependency context; stable spelling or an identifier does not establish current availability or authority.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.CLAIM_CLASS: Conditional engineering property derived from formal mechanisms and their boundaries
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.BEARER_OR_SUBJECT: Reference, scope/module graph, language resolution rules and source/dependency revision.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.FAILURE_MODE_OR_LIMIT_ADDRESSED: Early lookup misses an import edge; stale cached binding survives dependency change; an identifier has a binding but is illegal in the present local context.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MECHANISM: Construct qualified graph edges, apply path/priority/type rules, defer unstable queries until requisite information exists, and invalidate affected results after dependencies change.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Use stable-query scheduling/reference attributes or incremental fragments with explicit completion conditions; retain unresolved or stuck outcomes.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.EXPECTED_PAYOFF: Navigation, checking and refactoring operate on current referents instead of name coincidences.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.PAYOFF_EVIDENCE_NOT_JUST_RATIONALE: Mechanistic/formal support: Resolution is relative to graph completeness, language-specific rules, phase and module context; a stable symbol label is insufficient. No direct comparative engineering-payoff experiment for this whole reconstructed property is established.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: Names are imported, overloaded, generated, edited, separately compiled or resolved through cyclic dependencies.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.ALTERNATIVE_MECHANISMS: A closed file with flat unique declarations can use a simple versioned symbol table and full recomputation.

APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Names are imported, overloaded, generated, edited, separately compiled or resolved through cyclic dependencies.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Known non-trigger: No consumer relies on a name’s referent or availability in an evolving or modular context; for example, a fixed literal-only artifact contains no such references. Lower-cost option already recorded: A closed file with flat unique declarations can use a simple versioned symbol table and full recomputation. Applicability and evidence limit: A flat file that can change still has an evolving resolution context. A versioned symbol table and full recomputation can cheaply establish current resolution, but do not make the guard false when that resolution is relied upon.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ASSUMPTIONS_AND_PRECONDITIONS: Scope construction and priority rules reflect the language; all resolution-relevant context is present or flagged incomplete; cache dependency model is sound.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ENVIRONMENT_AND_BOUNDARY: Resolution is a language relation; current operational permission and stakeholder identity remain separate.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.SCOPE_AND_EXCLUSIONS: Resolution is relative to graph completeness, language-specific rules, phase and module context; a stable symbol label is insufficient.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.AUTHORITY_OR_NORMATIVE_BASIS_IF_APPLICAB: Source language definitions/theorems or tool contracts are authoritative only within their versioned scope. This reconstructed research property is not a normative requirement for any target.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.INPUT_AND_EVIDENCE_PROVENANCE_REQUIREMEN: Record exact input/model, language/tool version, dependencies, evaluator, observation method and source locators; separate constructed examples, source proofs and observed tool outcomes. Missing dependency, unfinished scope graph, overload constraints or cyclic analysis with no established fixed point.

DEPENDENCIES_AND_CONFLICTS.NOTE: Graphs do not remove circular dependencies; premature queries can be unstable, and stronger scheduling restrictions can reject workable language designs. Relations collection provides directional shared-bearer conditions.

APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.FAILURE_OF_ASSUMPTIONS: Early lookup misses an import edge; stale cached binding survives dependency change; an identifier has a binding but is illegal in the present local context. A missing premise produces UNKNOWN for the guarantee, not a fabricated PASS.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.COST_AND_MAINTENANCE_BURDEN: Cross-file dependencies, query scheduling, overload/type feedback, cycles and invalidation; more sophisticated graphs may not pay off for tiny programs.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: Context-dependent name resolution and revalidation: A reference is established by current language-specific resolution in its relevant dependency context; stable spelling or an identifier does not establish current availability or authority.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: For every admitted instance/transition explicitly covered by the stated rule and applicability guard; a worked example is not evidence for all programs. Resolution is a language relation; current operational permission and stakeholder identity remain separate.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: Reference, scope/module graph, language resolution rules and source/dependency revision.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Evaluate against the recorded version/environment; execution/transition statements range over the rule's modeled executions, while current evidence is a dated observation. resolve(r,G,rules,revision)=d is usable only if the result is stable under all still-permitted graph completions and valid in the required local/phase context; a changed dependency invalidates cached d until rechecked.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ASSUMPTIONS: Scope construction and priority rules reflect the language; all resolution-relevant context is present or flagged incomplete; cache dependency model is sound.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: A(r): a consumer relies on the referent or availability of r in an evolving/modular context.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE: resolve(r,G,rules,revision)=d is usable only if the result is stable under all still-permitted graph completions and valid in the required local/phase context; a changed dependency invalidates cached d until rechecked.

SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.NOTE: This operational rule is a synthesis for intake evaluation, not a formula quoted from a source theorem; source theorems remain bounded by their own language and hypotheses.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Construct from current source and declared module interfaces; Run language-specific lookup and record derivation/dependency set. Map these values into the rule without substituting a successful tool exit for semantic truth.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Scope construction and priority rules reflect the language; all resolution-relevant context is present or flagged incomplete; cache dependency model is sound. Required witness data: resolution_context and resolution_result.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: Run the language resolution procedure with dependency completion/scheduling checks; compare current declaration identity and availability; unresolved cycles remain UNKNOWN or a specified language error.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: The finite instance/trace checks described by the evaluator may be executable. Quantification over all programs, contexts or executions requires the source's restricted theorem/proof; finite testing is incomplete, and timeout yields UNKNOWN.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.POSITIVE_WITNESS: Constructed: resolve A.foo only after the import A and export foo are known, then invalidate the result when A changes.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: Published: Bessant/Van Wyk Figure 1 lookup y before its import edge is built is unstable. Racket also distinguishes a lexical binding from availability in the current local binding context.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: Missing dependency, unfinished scope graph, overload constraints or cyclic analysis with no established fixed point. Missing evidence is not evidence that the guard is false. If A is already known true, an unestablished model, premise, proof or coverage leaves the operational judgment UNKNOWN through P/E; if a fact needed to decide A itself is unknown, report A=UNKNOWN. Only an established false A permits INAPPLICABLE.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: No consumer relies on a name’s referent or availability in an evolving or modular context; for example, a fixed literal-only artifact contains no such references.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False positive: treating an incomplete boundary/proxy as the whole claim (Early lookup misses an import edge; stale cached binding survives dependency change; an identifier has a binding but is illegal in the present local context.). False negative: rejecting a valid instance because a conservative analysis or restricted proof language cannot express it; distinguish analyzer rejection from demonstrated semantic failure.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: A checker that rejects everything, empty accepted corpus, erased error nodes, or an observation model that omits the disputed behavior can make apparent success vacuous. Graphs do not remove circular dependencies; premature queries can be unstable, and stronger scheduling restrictions can reject workable language designs.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Import/export, binding, overload, scope/phase, dependency revision or graph-construction schedule changes.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Cross-file dependencies, query scheduling, overload/type feedback, cycles and invalidation; more sophisticated graphs may not pay off for tiny programs. Cheaper path: A closed file with flat unique declarations can use a simple versioned symbol table and full recomputation. Applicability and evidence limit: A flat file that can change still has an evolving resolution context. A versioned symbol table and full recomputation can cheaply establish current resolution, but do not make the guard false when that resolution is relied upon.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Soundness relative to a language-specific construction and restricted scheduling translation; no universal language-agnostic correctness from graph structure alone.

FORMALISATION_PROVENANCE.LIMIT: The intake predicate is not represented as a published universal theorem.

APPLICABILITY_A.TRUE: A(r): a consumer relies on the referent or availability of r in an evolving/modular context.
APPLICABILITY_A.FALSE: No consumer relies on a name’s referent or availability in an evolving or modular context; for example, a fixed literal-only artifact contains no such references.
APPLICABILITY_A.UNKNOWN: The truth of the applicability guard itself is not established. When the guard is known true, missing model/premise/proof/coverage evidence belongs to unresolved P/E and yields overall UNKNOWN, not A=false. Specific evidence gaps: Missing dependency, unfinished scope graph, overload constraints or cyclic analysis with no established fixed point.

PROPERTY_P.TRUE: The precise rule holds for the stated model/instance and quantified scope.
PROPERTY_P.FALSE: A counterexample within the guard violates the rule.
PROPERTY_P.UNDETERMINED: Truth is not settled by available observation or proof; it is not inferred from missing evidence.

OPERATIONAL_EVALUATION.CURRENT_EVALUATION: Schema and constructed witnesses only; no target instance was evaluated.

EVALUATOR_OUTCOMES.PASS: Adequate, current evidence establishes P for the declared scope and A is true.
EVALUATOR_OUTCOMES.FAIL: Adequate counterevidence establishes a violation with A true.
EVALUATOR_OUTCOMES.UNKNOWN: A or P is unresolved, evidence stale, solver times out or scope is incomplete.
EVALUATOR_OUTCOMES.INAPPLICABLE: No consumer relies on a name’s referent or availability in an evolving or modular context; for example, a fixed literal-only artifact contains no such references.

EVIDENCE_SUFFICIENCY_E.SIGNATURE: E_p(evidence, target={the named predicate=true or the named predicate=false}, scope) -> adequacy judgment
EVIDENCE_SUFFICIENCY_E.SUFFICIENT: The evidence, its provenance, coverage and evaluator soundness conditions justify that specifically named truth/falsity verdict in the declared scope.
EVIDENCE_SUFFICIENCY_E.INSUFFICIENT_OR_UNKNOWN: The required premise, observation, source/implementation bridge or evaluator coverage is missing or unresolved. This does not decide predicate truth.
EVIDENCE_SUFFICIENCY_E.NEGATIVE_WITNESS_RULE: A valid counterexample to the actual predicate can establish predicate=false with adequate evidence and overall evaluator FAIL. Evidence refuting only a stronger overclaim does not establish the retained predicate=false.
EVIDENCE_SUFFICIENCY_E.LIMIT: Adequacy for one target/scope does not establish a different predicate, unrestricted truth or the original candidate if the named predicate instead tests its critique.

EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.NEXT_DISCRIMINATOR: Run the language resolution procedure with dependency completion/scheduling checks; compare current declaration identity and availability; unresolved cycles remain UNKNOWN or a specified language error. Supply missing resolution_context / resolution_result evidence before strengthening the verdict.

RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: The generic negative-case verdict conflates failure of the retained predicate with failure of a stronger implication. XA10 gives a well-typed, safe function returning zero that violates an intended increment requirement; C0010-P01 deliberately claims only avoidance of Bad_L. XA12 gives a function satisfying its encoded postcondition result=0 but not the intended increment; C0012-P01 is the relative formal-specification claim. In both cases the retained predicate can remain true, yet EXPECTED_A_P_E.NEGATIVE assigns A=true, P=false and E=FAIL. The phrase for the precise violated rule/overclaim does not identify a separate overclaim predicate and leaves the case evaluator capable of falsely failing the retained property. Analogous ambiguity occurs where unauthorized effects, uncalibrated physical time or out-of-fragment seq refute only additional inferences.

Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: The finite instance/trace checks described by the evaluator may be executable. Quantification over all programs, contexts or executions requires the source's restricted theorem/proof; finite testing is incomplete, and timeout yields UNKNOWN.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.POSITIVE_WITNESS: Constructed: a small-step integer language includes explicit division error and infinite loop transitions; a safety predicate excludes only stated stuck states.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: Constructed: 0*f()→0 is unjustified in a call-by-value language if f prints or diverges, even though both fit the same arithmetic AST schema.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: Primitive semantics, environment assumptions or observation mapping not supplied; absence of a big-step derivation has no unique interpretation. Missing evidence is not evidence that the guard is false. If A is already known true, an unestablished model, premise, proof or coverage leaves the operational judgment UNKNOWN through P/E; if a fact needed to decide A itself is unknown, report A=UNKNOWN. PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False positive: treating an incomplete boundary/proxy as the whole claim (A terminating big-step result is mistaken for termination, missing outcomes conflated with safety, or a pure model used to justify effectful behavior.). False negative: rejecting a valid instance because a conservative analysis or restricted proof language cannot express it; distinguish analyzer rejection from demonstrated semantic failure.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: A checker that rejects everything, empty accepted corpus, erased error nodes, or an observation model that omits the disputed behavior can make apparent success vacuous. A formally precise but inadequate model can establish irrelevant properties; more detail can make proofs intractable without improving the decision.

APPLICABILITY_A.TRUE: A(M): a behavioral or proof conclusion is drawn from semantic model M.

APPLICABILITY_A.UNKNOWN: The truth of the applicability guard itself is not established. When the guard is known true, missing model/premise/proof/coverage evidence belongs to unresolved P/E and yields overall UNKNOWN, not A=false. Specific evidence gaps: Primitive semantics, environment assumptions or observation mapping not supplied; absence of a big-step derivation has no unique interpretation.

PROPERTY_P.TRUE: The precise rule holds for the stated model/instance and quantified scope.
PROPERTY_P.FALSE: A counterexample within the guard violates the rule.
PROPERTY_P.UNDETERMINED: Truth is not settled by available observation or proof; it is not inferred from missing evidence.

EVALUATOR_OUTCOMES.PASS: Adequate, current evidence establishes P for the declared scope and A is true.
EVALUATOR_OUTCOMES.FAIL: Adequate counterevidence establishes a violation with A true.
EVALUATOR_OUTCOMES.UNKNOWN: A or P is unresolved, evidence stale, solver times out or scope is incomplete.
EVALUATOR_OUTCOMES.INAPPLICABLE: No behavioral or proof conclusion is drawn from the assessed semantic model; for example, a tool reports only token spelling without a behavioral claim.

EVIDENCE_SUFFICIENCY_E.SUFFICIENT: The evidence, its provenance, coverage and evaluator soundness conditions justify that specifically named truth/falsity verdict in the declared scope.
EVIDENCE_SUFFICIENCY_E.INSUFFICIENT_OR_UNKNOWN: The required premise, observation, source/implementation bridge or evaluator coverage is missing or unresolved. This does not decide predicate truth.
EVIDENCE_SUFFICIENCY_E.NEGATIVE_WITNESS_RULE: A valid counterexample to the actual predicate can establish predicate=false with adequate evidence and overall evaluator FAIL. Evidence refuting only a stronger overclaim does not establish the retained predicate=false.
EVIDENCE_SUFFICIENCY_E.LIMIT: Adequacy for one target/scope does not establish a different predicate, unrestricted truth or the original candidate if the named predicate instead tests its critique.

RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: Several citation-ready entries print the mature modern claim but retain only the first three historical source links. Those displayed paths do not directly establish important parts of the printed claim, and one uses metadata-only Huet as though it supported a current transformation mechanism.

The generic negative-case verdict conflates failure of the retained predicate with failure of a stronger implication. XA10 gives a well-typed, safe function returning zero that violates an intended increment requirement; C0010-P01 deliberately claims only avoidance of Bad_L. XA12 gives a function satisfying its encoded postcondition result=0 but not the intended increment; C0012-P01 is the relative formal-specification claim. In both cases the retained predicate can remain true, yet EXPECTED_A_P_E.NEGATIVE assigns A=true, P=false and E=FAIL. The phrase for the precise violated rule/overclaim does not identify a separate overclaim predicate and leaves the case evaluator capable of falsely failing the retained property. Analogous ambiguity occurs where unauthorized effects, uncalibrated physical time or out-of-fragment seq refute only additional inferences.

Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: The generic negative-case verdict conflates failure of the retained predicate with failure of a stronger implication. XA10 gives a well-typed, safe function returning zero that violates an intended increment requirement; C0010-P01 deliberately claims only avoidance of Bad_L. XA12 gives a function satisfying its encoded postcondition result=0 but not the intended increment; C0012-P01 is the relative formal-specification claim. In both cases the retained predicate can remain true, yet EXPECTED_A_P_E.NEGATIVE assigns A=true, P=false and E=FAIL. The phrase for the precise violated rule/overclaim does not identify a separate overclaim predicate and leaves the case evaluator capable of falsely failing the retained property. Analogous ambiguity occurs where unauthorized effects, uncalibrated physical time or out-of-fragment seq refute only additional inferences.

Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.AUTHORITY_OR_NORMATIVE_BASIS_IF_APPLICAB: Source language definitions/theorems or tool contracts are authoritative only within their versioned scope. This reconstructed research property is not a normative requirement for any target.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: Claim-specific type soundness with an explicit trusted boundary: A type judgment supports only the failure-exclusion theorem proved for that language fragment, assumptions and trusted implementation boundary.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: For every admitted instance/transition explicitly covered by the stated rule and applicability guard; a worked example is not evidence for all programs. Defined stuck/type errors only. Divergence, permitted exceptions, arithmetic/fuel failures, functional intentions and unverified FFI may remain.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: A typed term/program, formal semantics, theorem and checker/foreign/unsafe boundary.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Evaluate against the recorded version/environment; execution/transition statements range over the rule's modeled executions, while current evidence is a dated observation. For fixed L, if Γ⊢p:T, the initial configuration satisfies theorem premises, all external/unsafe components meet their contracts, and the checker is sound for the judgment, then every modeled execution avoids Bad_L. Progress/preservation is one sufficient proof route; permitted errors must be listed separately.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ASSUMPTIONS: Typing rules and semantics align; the theorem handles the constructs used; primitive/callee/initial-state assumptions hold; checker output corresponds to a formal derivation.

SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION.NOTE: This operational rule is a synthesis for intake evaluation, not a formula quoted from a source theorem; source theorems remain bounded by their own language and hypotheses.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Inspect judgment and formal theorem, not the phrase type safe; Match constructs and checker/runtime versions to the theorem and inspect escape contracts. Map these values into the rule without substituting a successful tool exit for semantic truth.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Typing rules and semantics align; the theorem handles the constructs used; primitive/callee/initial-state assumptions hold; checker output corresponds to a formal derivation. Required witness data: type_guarantee_contract and trusted_boundary.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: Check derivation/theorem premises and artifact correspondence; a typed source plus unverified executable mapping yields UNKNOWN at deployment boundary, not a theorem failure.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: The finite instance/trace checks described by the evaluator may be executable. Quantification over all programs, contexts or executions requires the source's restricted theorem/proof; finite testing is incomplete, and timeout yields UNKNOWN.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.POSITIVE_WITNESS: Constructed: closed simply typed arithmetic with a preservation/progress proof excludes application of an integer as a function.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: Constructed: a well-typed int→int function returning 0 violates an intended increment requirement. Published MoveLight theorem permits division-by-zero/abort/fuel errors while excluding its preventable classes.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: Type checker accepted but theorem fragment, unsafe contract, initial assumptions or binary correspondence unavailable. Missing evidence is not evidence that the guard is false. If A is already known true, an unestablished model, premise, proof or coverage leaves the operational judgment UNKNOWN through P/E; if a fact needed to decide A itself is unknown, report A=UNKNOWN. Only an established false A permits INAPPLICABLE.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: No type judgment is used to support an execution-safety conclusion; for example, type-shaped labels are displayed only as documentation with no safety inference.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False positive: treating an incomplete boundary/proxy as the whole claim (Well-typedness promoted to total functional/security/timing correctness, or unsafe libraries, casts/FFI and runtime failures omitted from the claim.). False negative: rejecting a valid instance because a conservative analysis or restricted proof language cannot express it; distinguish analyzer rejection from demonstrated semantic failure.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: A checker that rejects everything, empty accepted corpus, erased error nodes, or an observation model that omits the disputed behavior can make apparent success vacuous. A sound theorem for a small calculus may say little about a deployed system; one can weaken the definition of error until the claim is unhelpful.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Language-specific metatheory, checker trust, unsafe abstraction proofs, invalidation after extensions and type-error explanation. RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: The inspected foundations narrative stops after the semantics branch. It gives no substantive branch treatment of type systems or effects/resources/protocols, despite declaring B02–B08 coverage and 24 resolved properties. These records exist in a.json but C13 requires an integrated argument in the human report, not only ledger rows.

The generic negative-case verdict conflates failure of the retained predicate with failure of a stronger implication. XA10 gives a well-typed, safe function returning zero that violates an intended increment requirement; C0010-P01 deliberately claims only avoidance of Bad_L. XA12 gives a function satisfying its encoded postcondition result=0 but not the intended increment; C0012-P01 is the relative formal-specification claim. In both cases the retained predicate can remain true, yet EXPECTED_A_P_E.NEGATIVE assigns A=true, P=false and E=FAIL. The phrase for the precise violated rule/overclaim does not identify a separate overclaim predicate and leaves the case evaluator capable of falsely failing the retained property. Analogous ambiguity occurs where unauthorized effects, uncalibrated physical time or out-of-fragment seq refute only additional inferences.

Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

REVIEW_FINDINGS_AND_DISPOSITION.LIMIT: No listed finding is not a guarantee of correctness; reviewers and their sampled documentary checks are described in the validation report.

No claim that a proof, parser, graph, type, capability label or static check establishes natural-language intention without a separate validated bridge.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Classify syntax and annotation form against the stated theorem; Run versioned algorithm with declared budget; retain result and diagnostic trace. Map these values into the rule without substituting a successful tool exit for semantic truth.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Term is in the proved applicative/let fragment; environment/generalization conditions hold; recursive/effectful extensions are not silently imported. Required witness data: inference_problem and inference_result_and_cost.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: Use a checked derivation and fragment-specific soundness/completeness theorem; measure actual inference costs without extrapolating asymptotic lower bounds to ordinary programs.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: The finite instance/trace checks described by the evaluator may be executable. Quantification over all programs, contexts or executions requires the source's restricted theorem/proof; finite testing is incomplete, and timeout yields UNKNOWN.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.POSITIVE_WITNESS: Constructed: let id=λx.x in (id true,id 1) admits the expected let-polymorphic instances in the standard pure fragment.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS: Constructed: treating lambda-bound f as let-polymorphic in λf.(f true,f 1) changes the discipline; unrestricted Curry-style System F inference has a different undecidable problem.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: Fragment membership or environment generalization unknown; algorithm resource limit reached or unsupported extension encountered. Missing evidence is not evidence that the guard is false. If A is already known true, an unestablished model, premise, proof or coverage leaves the operational judgment UNKNOWN through P/E; if a fact needed to decide A itself is unknown, report A=UNKNOWN. Only an established false A permits INAPPLICABLE.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: Neither automatic type synthesis nor a principalness claim is requested for the assessed expression; for example, supplied annotations are checked with no inference or principal-type assertion.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False positive: treating an incomplete boundary/proxy as the whole claim (Assuming all polymorphism has decidable inference, or inferring that a decidable algorithm is predictably cheap.). False negative: rejecting a valid instance because a conservative analysis or restricted proof language cannot express it; distinguish analyzer rejection from demonstrated semantic failure.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: A checker that rejects everything, empty accepted corpus, erased error nodes, or an observation model that omits the disputed behavior can make apparent success vacuous. Principal inference trades expressiveness and worst-case tractability; a safe program can be untypable in the chosen discipline.
