records.title: Carry semantic assumptions through the runtime and actual executable boundary

IDENTITY.PROPERTY_NAME: Carry semantic assumptions through the runtime and actual executable boundary

GENEALOGY.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Runtime systems extend the operational meaning of compiled programs. Verified CakeML collector/backend work enlarges correspondence to runtime and bytes; CoreJIT models speculation/deoptimization, FM-JIT adds native-code execution and effectful primitives; mechanized WebAssembly interpreters provide executable reference semantics and testing oracles.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_TERMINOLOGY: Simulation/refinement; installation; GC roots; JIT guard/deoptimization; extraction; interpreter soundness; trusted primitive
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_FORM: Ensure the implementation executing the language obeys the abstract semantics across representation, memory and control transitions.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_PROBLEM: Successful compilation or an elegant source semantics can omit actual parser/numerics, allocation, GC, exceptions, native callbacks, dynamic code, OS and resource behavior.

HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE_AND_LOCATORS.LOCATOR: Root validity; gc_related; generational invariant and integration
Fig.7 compile theorem; installed; extend_with_resource_limit; top-level frontend theorem; §11
Speculative assumptions; synchronization points; restoration of baseline execution

GENEALOGY.DISPUTED_ATTRIBUTION_OR_ANACHRONISM_RISK: Do not project current features, proof coverage or terminology backwards onto earlier versions.
GENEALOGY.RELATION_CLASS_EXPLANATION: Detailed dated historical/analytical edges are in genealogy_edges; this record summarizes qualified present evolution and does not claim every cited source influenced every other source.

CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.ENGINEERING_CLAIM: An implementation correspondence claim must identify concrete endpoints and every runtime transition that can affect its observations, separating proved components from specifications, axioms, wrappers and tested primitives.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.BEARER_OR_SUBJECT: executing compiler/interpreter/VM/runtime and its relation to the modeled semantics
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.FAILURE_MODE_OR_LIMIT_ADDRESSED: Successful compilation or an elegant source semantics can omit actual parser/numerics, allocation, GC, exceptions, native callbacks, dynamic code, OS and resource behavior.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MECHANISM: Relate concrete states/traces to semantic states, compose compiler/interpreter/runtime simulations, and establish installation/FFI/primitive contracts. Runtime guards and deoptimization maps discharge speculative assumptions only within their proved model.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Verified collectors and byte encoders enlarge endpoints; effectful JIT models expose native primitives; verified interpreters can act as differential-test oracles while maintaining an explicit parser/numerics/extraction boundary.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.EXPECTED_PAYOFF: Locate failures that source-only reasoning misses and make assurance compositional across runtime stages.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.PAYOFF_EVIDENCE_NOT_JUST_RATIONALE: CakeML and FM-JIT provide model correspondence theorems; WasmRef-Isabelle has a mechanized efficient interpreter and was used in Wasmtime fuzzing. Each has explicit trusted/unsupported boundaries, and partial correctness/resource exits limit availability claims.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: A language implementer or deployer relying on a semantic theorem for the actual executing artifact.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.ALTERNATIVE_MECHANISMS: A small constrained interpreter with a narrow trusted boundary; execute a specification directly; isolate foreign code; bounded conformance/differential testing when a universal theorem is unnecessary.

APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Execution depends on compiler/runtime/VM behavior beyond the abstract source language, especially GC, JIT, foreign interfaces, resource limits or platform numerics.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Known non-trigger: The claim is confined to an abstract language/model and asserts no result depending on a concrete compiler, runtime or VM beyond that model; for example, a mathematical reduction theorem makes no actual-execution claim. Lower-cost option already recorded: For a bounded arithmetic/data DSL, a small reviewed interpreter with explicit input/resource limits may be adequate without a optimizing native compiler, speculative JIT or elaborate runtime. Applicability and evidence limit: A small reviewed interpreter is still an implementation boundary when actual execution is claimed. Its size can make the primitive, initialization and observation correspondence argument cheaper. It receives PASS only if the exact scoped implementation relation is established; review or a few tests alone do not establish an unbounded theorem.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ASSUMPTIONS_AND_PRECONDITIONS: Actual code and installation match theorem endpoints; runtime/foreign primitives realize specifications; numerical representation/rounding, memory/resource limits, OS interactions, extraction and platform semantics meet stated premises.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ENVIRONMENT_AND_BOUNDARY: Named source/intermediate/assembly/byte models, interpreter return outcomes, collector/FFI contracts and physical execution boundary; each example has different endpoints.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.SCOPE_AND_EXCLUSIONS: Specified observable behavior/refinement, often permitting failure, divergence or resource-limit exits under model rules. Excludes: Guaranteed successful deployment, total correctness from a partial interpreter theorem, all actual FP/SIMD behavior from opaque model functions, or combined JIT features whose proofs were developed separately.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.AUTHORITY_OR_NORMATIVE_BASIS_IF_APPLICAB: Conditional semantic/mechanistic result. No universal mandate or legal authority is inferred.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.INPUT_AND_EVIDENCE_PROVENANCE_REQUIREMEN: Exact implementation/model versions and endpoints; proof statements and axioms; initial installation and primitive contracts; unsupported-feature list; independent current correspondence/test evidence for remaining layers.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.DEPENDENCIES_AND_CONFLICTS: EPLT-C0106–EPLT-C0109 translation/certificate boundaries; EPLT-C0110 foreign contracts; EPLT-C0112–EPLT-C0113 scheduling/memory; EPLT-C0114–EPLT-C0115 version/currentness; EPLT-C0117 separates testing/reproducibility.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.FAILURE_OF_ASSUMPTIONS: C primitive implements a finite stack while proof model assumes unbounded storage; decoder accepts a mismodeled instruction; unmanaged pointer survives GC incorrectly; rounding mode changes while source model assumes a fixed mode.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.COST_AND_MAINTENANCE_BURDEN: Runtime model complexity and proof maintenance, low-level installation/environment assurance and restrictions on unsupported features; a smaller execution stack reduces obligations.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.RETIREMENT_OR_REENTRY_CONDITION: Recheck after changing runtime/VM, primitive implementations, GC, numeric backend, parser, extraction settings, OS/ISA, resource policies, JIT guards/deoptimization or foreign code.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: Every implementation behavior admitted by the theorem’s execution/primitive model from related initial states; actual hardware enters only through an established realization relation.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: executing compiler/interpreter/VM/runtime and its relation to the modeled semantics
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Whole execution behavior unless the explicit relation below restricts the observation to states or finite traces.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ASSUMPTIONS: Actual code and installation match theorem endpoints; runtime/foreign primitives realize specifications; numerical representation/rounding, memory/resource limits, OS interactions, extraction and platform semantics meet stated premises.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: Execution depends on compiler/runtime/VM behavior beyond the abstract source language, especially GC, JIT, foreign interfaces, resource limits or platform numerics.

EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE.A: Execution depends on compiler/runtime/VM behavior beyond the abstract source language, especially GC, JIT, foreign interfaces, resource limits or platform numerics.
EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE.P: InitRelated ∧ PrimitiveRel ∧ ImplementationPremises ⇒ ∀bI∈BehI. ∃bM∈BehM. ObsI(bI) R ObsM(bM). If R includes resource/crash outcomes or theorem is partial, no success/termination guarantee follows without an additional premise/theorem.
EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE.E: Exact implementation/model versions and endpoints; proof statements and axioms; initial installation and primitive contracts; unsupported-feature list; independent current correspondence/test evidence for remaining layers.
EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE.VERDICT_RULE: Evaluate A (applicability), P (claim truth) and E (evidence adequacy) separately. A=FAIL gives INAPPLICABLE, never a vacuous pass. A=UNKNOWN or required E missing gives UNKNOWN. For A=PASS, sound proof/complete scoped check supports PASS; a valid scoped counterexample gives FAIL; timeout, unsupported features, heuristic failure or incomplete coverage give UNKNOWN. E=FAIL denotes a known mismatch between evidence and bearer, not automatic semantic falsity.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION: Researcher composition of simulation/refinement structure; FM-JIT’s backward-simulation statement, CakeML resource-extension relation and WasmRef interpreter partial-correctness outcome are distinguished in the profile.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: Results, I/O, exceptions and modeled failure/divergence; timing, allocation and physical behavior are included only if the relation observes them.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: Exact implementation/model versions and endpoints; proof statements and axioms; initial installation and primitive contracts; unsupported-feature list; independent current correspondence/test evidence for remaining layers.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: Trace one actual execution across parser/compiler/runtime boundaries, inspect each correspondence obligation and challenge a trusted primitive/resource assumption. A proof for one intermediate layer does not fill the rest.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: Whole-implementation correspondence is generally undecidable; mechanized simulations and restricted component checkers establish scoped results. Finite conformance tests cannot prove universal coverage.

POSITIVE_WITNESS.WITNESS: Source-grounded: CakeML collector/root invariants and backend relations cover allocation/collection under the model. CoreJIT guards plus explicit deoptimization maps restore baseline state when speculative assumptions fail.

COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS.WITNESS: Source-grounded boundary: FM-JIT’s stack specification is unbounded while its C implementation uses a finite array; the theorem does not establish arbitrary resource sufficiency. Constructed: compilation succeeds but a C callback omits a GC root and later dereferences a relocated object.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: Missing semantics/configuration, unsupported constructs or unavailable proof/check results leave the claim UNKNOWN. Missing evidence is not evidence that the guard is false. If A is already known true, an unestablished model, premise, proof or coverage leaves the operational judgment UNKNOWN through P/E; if a fact needed to decide A itself is unknown, report A=UNKNOWN. Only an established false A permits INAPPLICABLE.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: The claim is confined to an abstract language/model and asserts no result depending on a concrete compiler, runtime or VM beyond that model; for example, a mathematical reduction theorem makes no actual-execution claim.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: An incomplete observation map can produce a false assurance; conservative rejection can withhold a true claim. Neither is resolved by a favorable label.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: Check a nonempty intended input/context class and actual successful executions; rejecting every input or observing nothing cannot establish usefulness.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Recheck after changing runtime/VM, primitive implementations, GC, numeric backend, parser, extraction settings, OS/ISA, resource policies, JIT guards/deoptimization or foreign code.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Runtime model complexity and proof maintenance, low-level installation/environment assurance and restrictions on unsupported features; a smaller execution stack reduces obligations. Cheaper path: For a bounded arithmetic/data DSL, a small reviewed interpreter with explicit input/resource limits may be adequate without a optimizing native compiler, speculative JIT or elaborate runtime. Applicability and evidence limit: A small reviewed interpreter is still an implementation boundary when actual execution is claimed. Its size can make the primitive, initialization and observation correspondence argument cheaper. It receives PASS only if the exact scoped implementation relation is established; review or a few tests alone do not establish an unbounded theorem.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVIDENCE_CEILING: The exact behavior relation at proved endpoints with explicit primitive/installation/resource assumptions.

RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.ENGINEERING_CLAIM: Original candidate H claims that reproducible bytes or green finite nonexhaustive tests suffice for universal implementation correctness. The research conclusion rejects H by explicit counterexamples. EPLT-C0117-P01 evaluates H itself, so those counterexamples yield FAIL; that predicate verdict supports the separate rejected research disposition. Reproducibility establishes identity under its build conditions, while finite passing tests establish observed behavior. Their valid narrower uses are preserved.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.BEARER_OR_SUBJECT: implementation, finite test corpus and build outputs alleged to establish a universal semantic theorem
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.FAILURE_MODE_OR_LIMIT_ADDRESSED: Evidence about byte identity or finitely many executions is promoted to an unbounded semantic correctness proposition.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MECHANISM: Expose the quantifier mismatch by constructing an implementation that agrees on every tested input but differs elsewhere, or a deterministic/reproducible implementation that always computes the wrong value.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Keep separate claims for provenance/byte identity, tested conformance, bounded validation and universal theorem. Passing exhaustive checking of a genuinely finite admitted domain can establish correctness restricted to that domain, provided the oracle is faithful and every relevant environment is covered. This is a separate proposition, not a PASS witness for H.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.EXPECTED_PAYOFF: Prevent false assurance while preserving the practical value of reproducibility, fuzzing and conformance checks for their own claims.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.PAYOFF_EVIDENCE_NOT_JUST_RATIONALE: Logical counterexamples refute the general implication. WasmRef oracle use and MixTesting findings demonstrate valuable testing without claiming completeness; Alive2 states bounded-loop limits. Root historical incidents provide additional empirical context, not the logical basis of rejection.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.DECISION_OR_CONSUMER: A reviewer deciding what a green build/test receipt actually supports.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.ALTERNATIVE_MECHANISMS: State the finite observation honestly; use a sound complete checker for the admitted domain; prove implementation correspondence; combine testing with model/boundary review.

APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: A byte-identity result or finite test result is offered as sufficient evidence of an unbounded all-programs implementation-correctness claim.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Known non-trigger: The actual question concerns only byte identity, observed finite conformance, or complete checking of a genuinely finite domain with an adequate oracle. Those different targets are not H and do not receive PASS under this predicate. Lower-cost option already recorded: If the only requirement is byte-for-byte reproducibility, compare bytes under declared build inputs. If the complete admitted input domain is finite and small, exhaustive evaluation with a trustworthy oracle can be adequate. Applicability and evidence limit: Byte comparison can establish a byte-identity target, and exhaustive finite-domain checking with an adequate oracle can establish its separate finite target. Neither is PASS for the original universal H. When H is the target, a validated refutation has E=PASS, P=FAIL and overall FAIL; missing or invalid evidence yields UNKNOWN. Preserve the existing AD002 target, Ω and verdict rules.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ASSUMPTIONS_AND_PRECONDITIONS: The rejected proposition quantifies beyond the observed test domain or confuses byte identity with semantic truth. The finite-domain exception requires actual exhaustive domain coverage, a faithful oracle and all relevant environment states.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ENVIRONMENT_AND_BOUNDARY: Evidence interpretation rather than a new compiler mechanism. Test runner/oracle correctness and implementation environments are independent premises.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.SCOPE_AND_EXCLUSIONS: Logical rejection of two general implications, preserving proper narrower uses of their antecedents. Excludes: Claiming tests are useless, reproducibility has no provenance value, or exhaustive finite-domain checking can never prove a scoped proposition.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.AUTHORITY_OR_NORMATIVE_BASIS_IF_APPLICAB: Conditional semantic/mechanistic result. No universal mandate or legal authority is inferred.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.INPUT_AND_EVIDENCE_PROVENANCE_REQUIREMEN: Exact advertised conclusion and evidence domain, complete-domain argument if claimed, oracle/runner assumptions, and a concrete counterexample outside observed scope for refutation.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.DEPENDENCIES_AND_CONFLICTS: EPLT-C0108 distinguishes bounded validation from unbounded proof; EPLT-C0115 distinguishes cache identity/currentness; EPLT-C0116 distinguishes tested residual components from proved correspondence. Root EPLT-C0308 overlaps only the finite-test clause.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.FAILURE_OF_ASSUMPTIONS: Any untested admitted input/environment can host a counterexample; a repeatable wrong compiler still yields identical wrong bytes.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.COST_AND_MAINTENANCE_BURDEN: Keeping evidence dimensions distinct adds little runtime cost; stronger universal assurance may require substantial proof/model work and should be demanded only when the claim needs it.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.RETIREMENT_OR_REENTRY_CONDITION: Recompute test/identity evidence when its inputs change; never widen its quantified domain without new coverage or proof. A genuinely finite exhaustive domain can change the judgment.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.NAME_AND_PLAIN_LANGUAGE_CLAIM: Original candidate H: for every admitted configuration, reproducible build output or a green finite nonexhaustive test suite suffices for semantic correctness on every admitted program, input and environment.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.SUBJECT_AND_ARGUMENT_SIGNATURE: H(Ω), where Ω is the original class of specification/domain/implementation/build/test configurations c=(S,D,I,B,T).
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS: S specifies allowed semantic observations; D is a nonempty admitted domain of program/input/environment instances and may be unbounded; I is an implementation; B is a build procedure under declared fixed inputs/configuration; T is a nonempty finite proper subset of D. Ω includes the elementary total-function configurations D=ℕ used in W_R and W_T. Byte strings and semantic observations are different value domains.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.QUANTIFIERS_AND_SCOPE: H quantifies over every configuration c∈Ω and every admitted instance x∈D. Its test disjunct quantifies only over the finite proper subset T. The same target H includes both original clauses: universally, reproducibility implies all-domain correctness; universally, green finite nonexhaustive tests imply all-domain correctness. Refuting either clause makes H false.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.STATE_TRACE_EVENT_OR_MODEL_BEARER: The original universal inference over configurations Ω, not the truth of the negative research conclusion and not a single correct implementation.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.TEMPORAL_AND_MODAL_SEMANTICS: Correct_S relates the implementation’s admitted observations to S under the declared execution semantics. Reproducible concerns repeated builds under fixed conditions, while Green concerns the specified finite executions. Neither observation changes H’s all-configuration/all-instance quantifiers. The counterexamples use terminating deterministic functions and require no liveness premise.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.ASSUMPTIONS: The semantics and observation relation are fixed, Ω includes W_R and W_T, and each tested result is checked by an adequate oracle. Nonempty finite T is a proper subset of D. No universal correctness or exclusion of erroneous implementations is assumed. Reproducible(B,I) means every admitted rebuild under the declared fixed inputs emits the same bytes denoting I; even this stronger reproducibility premise is insufficient.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.APPLICABILITY_GUARD: The claim being assessed is the original universal evidence-promotion hypothesis H over the declared configuration class Ω. It offers reproducibility or passing a finite nonexhaustive suite as sufficient for semantic correctness on every admitted instance. A claim restricted to byte identity, observed tests or an exhaustively covered finite domain is a different target.

EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE.A: The claim being assessed is the original universal evidence-promotion hypothesis H over the declared configuration class Ω. It offers reproducibility or passing a finite nonexhaustive suite as sufficient for semantic correctness on every admitted instance. A claim restricted to byte identity, observed tests or an exhaustively covered finite domain is a different target.
EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE.DEFINITIONS: Green_S(I,T) := ∀t∈T.Pass_S(I,t), with each Pass established by the stated adequate oracle. Correct_S(I,x) is the declared semantic correspondence relation. Reproducible(B,I) is the repeatable-byte property under the declared build conditions. Ω and T’s nonempty finite proper-subset condition are fixed in VARIABLE_DOMAINS_AND_UNITS and ASSUMPTIONS.
EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE.E: For PASS, a sound argument proving H over all of its original Ω. For FAIL, a validated configuration in Ω with at least one true antecedent disjunct and a concrete x∈D for which Correct_S(I,x) is false. Record the specification, domain, implementation, build conditions or complete finite test set, oracle, and semantic mismatch. A mere lack of proof or test coverage is not this counterexample.
EXPRESSION_OR_PRECISE_OPERATIONAL_RULE.VERDICT_RULE: Evaluate A, truth of H, and adequacy E separately. A=FAIL gives INAPPLICABLE; an ambiguous target or A=UNKNOWN gives UNKNOWN. For A=PASS and E=PASS, a valid proof of H gives P=PASS/overall PASS; a validated counterexample with a true antecedent and false semantic consequent gives P=FAIL/overall FAIL. A successfully validated refutation therefore has E=PASS and P=FAIL. Missing, invalid or bearer-mismatched evidence (E=MISSING, UNKNOWN or FAIL), incomplete search or lack of a proof gives overall UNKNOWN, not semantic FAIL. A false antecedent at one configuration or a true implication at one configuration does not establish the universal H.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.SOURCE_OF_THE_EXPRESSION: Researcher elementary logical counterexample to evidence promotion; boundedness and trust distinctions corroborated by inspected primary sources. Not a theorem attributed to a tool’s authors.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.OBSERVATION_OR_MEASUREMENT_MAP: First establish the relevant antecedent: reproducible bytes under B or all oracle-checked tests in T. Then compare I’s behavior with S at the same admitted configuration and witness x. Byte equality is not a semantic relation; finite green observations do not themselves determine Correct_S outside T.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.REQUIRED_EVIDENCE: For PASS, a sound argument proving H over all of its original Ω. For FAIL, a validated configuration in Ω with at least one true antecedent disjunct and a concrete x∈D for which Correct_S(I,x) is false. Record the specification, domain, implementation, build conditions or complete finite test set, oracle, and semantic mismatch. A mere lack of proof or test coverage is not this counterexample.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATOR_OR_REASONING_PROCEDURE: Fix the original Ω and H. Validate W_R by the definitions of the constant build and constant-wrong function; validate W_T by checking the complete T={0} and the semantic mismatch at 1. Each establishes a true antecedent and false consequent in Ω, so E=PASS, P=FAIL and the overall verdict is FAIL. This rejects the original candidate. Evaluate byte equality or exhaustive finite-domain controls under their own propositions, never as replacements for H.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.DECIDABILITY_AND_APPROXIMATION: The displayed counterexamples admit direct mathematical checking. Finite byte comparisons and completed finite test observations can be checked, but general all-program semantic correspondence is undecidable without restrictions; a test may also fail to terminate. No complete generic decision procedure for H is claimed.

POSITIVE_WITNESS.WITNESS: No PASS witness is supplied for H: the configurations W_R and W_T refute that original universal candidate. A correct implementation or a valid narrower byte-identity/finite-domain theorem is not a PASS witness for H over all Ω. Such controls are recorded separately under QUALIFIED_ALTERNATIVES_AND_CONTROLS without changing the predicate target.

COUNTEREXAMPLE_OR_FAILURE_WITNESS.WITNESS: W_R: let D=ℕ, S(n)=1 for every n, T={0}, and I_R(n)=0 for every n. Define B_R to emit the same bytes denoting I_R on every admitted rebuild under its fixed inputs. Reproducible(B_R,I_R) is true, Green_S(I_R,T) is false, and Correct_S(I_R,0) is false. The reproducibility disjunct therefore refutes H. W_T: let D=ℕ, S(n)=1 for every n, T={0}, and I_T(n)=1 when n=0 and 0 otherwise. With an adequate oracle, Green_S(I_T,T) is true, but Correct_S(I_T,1) is false. The finite-test disjunct therefore refutes H regardless of whether the build is reproducible. These are analytical constructions, not executions or defect allegations about a cited compiler.

PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.UNKNOWN_CONDITIONS: An ambiguous candidate/domain, missing semantics or configuration, or an invalid/unverifiable proposed counterexample makes that assessment UNKNOWN. Merely identifying an untested input without showing wrong behavior does not itself yield FAIL. These limits do not undo the explicit analytical refutation of the original H by W_R and W_T. Missing evidence is not evidence that the guard is false. If A is already known true, an unestablished model, premise, proof or coverage leaves the operational judgment UNKNOWN through P/E; if a fact needed to decide A itself is unknown, report A=UNKNOWN. Only an established false A permits INAPPLICABLE.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS: The actual question concerns only byte identity, observed finite conformance, or complete checking of a genuinely finite domain with an adequate oracle. Those different targets are not H and do not receive PASS under this predicate.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.FALSE_POSITIVE_AND_FALSE_NEGATIVE_RISKS: False PASS: treating a successful refutation, one correct implementation, equal bytes, or a green suite as proof of H. False FAIL: treating missing proof, incomplete testing, or an invalid/mismatched counterexample as semantic refutation. Require the explicit H target and A/P/E separation.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.VACUITY_OR_PROXY_GAMING_RISKS: Do not shrink Ω to known-correct implementations, replace H with ¬H, or treat a false antecedent as proof of the universal. T is nonempty and proper; one vacuously true local implication or one narrower theorem cannot establish H.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.CHANGE_INVALIDATION_RULE: Recompute test/identity evidence when its inputs change; never widen its quantified domain without new coverage or proof. A genuinely finite exhaustive domain can change the judgment.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.COST_AND_CHEAPER_ALTERNATIVE: Keeping evidence dimensions distinct adds little runtime cost; stronger universal assurance may require substantial proof/model work and should be demanded only when the claim needs it. Cheaper path: If the only requirement is byte-for-byte reproducibility, compare bytes under declared build inputs. If the complete admitted input domain is finite and small, exhaustive evaluation with a trustworthy oracle can be adequate. Applicability and evidence limit: Byte comparison can establish a byte-identity target, and exhaustive finite-domain checking with an adequate oracle can establish its separate finite target. Neither is PASS for the original universal H. When H is the target, a validated refutation has E=PASS, P=FAIL and overall FAIL; missing or invalid evidence yields UNKNOWN. Preserve the existing AD002 target, Ω and verdict rules.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Logical invalidity of the broad implication plus source-specific evidence-scope observations; not a numerical defect-rate estimate.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.RELATION_TO_CANDIDATE: DIRECT_TEST_OF_ORIGINAL_CANDIDATE_H. Evaluate H itself, not ¬H and not Refutes(w,H). The separate research disposition REJECTED_OR_DISFAVOURED follows from H receiving FAIL on adequate counterexample evidence.
PREDICATE_SPECIFICATIONS.EVALUATOR_PASS_MEANING: PASS means H has been established over the full original Ω. It never means that a refutation was successfully checked, that one implementation is correct, that bytes match, or that a narrower finite-domain theorem holds.

QUALIFIED_ALTERNATIVES_AND_CONTROLS.PROPOSITION: Two declared build outputs are byte-for-byte equal.
QUALIFIED_ALTERNATIVES_AND_CONTROLS.EVIDENCE_AND_RESULT: Direct equality comparison can establish this identity proposition under its stated inputs; no semantic correctness follows from equality alone.
QUALIFIED_ALTERNATIVES_AND_CONTROLS.RELATION_TO_H: A different, narrower proposition; INAPPLICABLE as an assessment of H and never a PASS witness for H.

QUALIFIED_ALTERNATIVES_AND_CONTROLS.PROPOSITION: For a genuinely finite D_f, complete coverage of all admitted inputs and environments, a faithful oracle, and ∀x∈D_f.Pass_S(I,x) imply ∀x∈D_f.Correct_S(I,x).
QUALIFIED_ALTERNATIVES_AND_CONTROLS.EVIDENCE_AND_RESULT: An adequate exhaustive check can establish this restricted correctness proposition. Domain completeness, oracle fidelity and every passing result are separate premises.
QUALIFIED_ALTERNATIVES_AND_CONTROLS.RELATION_TO_H: A different, narrower proposition outside H’s nonexhaustive-test inference; it does not prove H or change EPLT-C0117’s rejected disposition.

ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.FORMALISATION_PROVENANCE: Researcher elementary logical counterexample to evidence promotion; boundedness and trust distinctions corroborated by inspected primary sources. Not a theorem attributed to a tool’s authors.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.OPERATIONAL_EVALUATION: Check quantifier/domain alignment; choose an untested input and construct two implementations identical on T but different there. For finite-domain claims, verify complete enumeration and adequate oracle. No target implementation was supplied or certified by this research. A/P/E are evaluation obligations, not computed owner-system scores. Applicability clarification: INAPPLICABLE only when The actual question concerns only byte identity, observed finite conformance, or complete checking of a genuinely finite domain with an adequate oracle. Those different targets are not H and do not receive PASS under this predicate. Cheap-path judgment: Byte comparison can establish a byte-identity target, and exhaustive finite-domain checking with an adequate oracle can establish its separate finite target. Neither is PASS for the original universal H. When H is the target, a validated refutation has E=PASS, P=FAIL and overall FAIL; missing or invalid evidence yields UNKNOWN. Preserve the existing AD002 target, Ω and verdict rules. Missing evidence is not evidence that the guard is false. If A is already known true, an unestablished model, premise, proof or coverage leaves the operational judgment UNKNOWN through P/E; if a fact needed to decide A itself is unknown, report A=UNKNOWN. Only an established false A permits INAPPLICABLE.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.POSITIVE_WITNESS_OR_WORKED_EXAMPLE: There is no positive witness for the rejected universal inference. Proper narrower case: two builds yield equal bytes, establishing that equality; or every input in a genuinely finite fully enumerated domain is checked with an adequate oracle, establishing only that restricted claim.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.NEGATIVE_WITNESS_OR_COUNTEREXAMPLE: Constructed: a deterministic build always emits a program returning0 when the required semantics returns1; it is perfectly reproducible. For finite nonexhaustive T, define I to behave correctly on T and return a wrong result for p* outside T; all tests pass and the universal claim is false.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.NON_TRIGGER_EXAMPLE: The actual question concerns only byte identity, observed finite conformance, or complete checking of a genuinely finite domain with an adequate oracle. Those different targets are not H and do not receive PASS under this predicate.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.OBSERVABILITY_AND_MISSINGNESS: Missing semantics/configuration, unsupported constructs or unavailable proof/check results leave the claim UNKNOWN.
ATTRIBUTES_AND_PREDICATES.CURRENTNESS_AND_INVALIDATION: Recompute test/identity evidence when its inputs change; never widen its quantified domain without new coverage or proof. A genuinely finite exhaustive domain can change the judgment.

CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.STRONGEST_OBJECTION: Universal semantic truth does not follow from a proposition about repeatability or a finite sample. Confidence and falsification value are not logical entailment.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.KNOWN_FAILURES_AND_MISUSES: W_R: let D=ℕ, S(n)=1 for every n, T={0}, and I_R(n)=0 for every n. Define B_R to emit the same bytes denoting I_R on every admitted rebuild under its fixed inputs. Reproducible(B_R,I_R) is true, Green_S(I_R,T) is false, and Correct_S(I_R,0) is false. The reproducibility disjunct therefore refutes H. W_T: let D=ℕ, S(n)=1 for every n, T={0}, and I_T(n)=1 when n=0 and 0 otherwise. With an adequate oracle, Green_S(I_T,T) is true, but Correct_S(I_T,1) is false. The finite-test disjunct therefore refutes H regardless of whether the build is reproducible. These are analytical constructions, not executions or defect allegations about a cited compiler.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.RESPONSE_OR_DESCENDANT_FORM: Keep separate claims for provenance/byte identity, tested conformance, bounded validation and universal theorem. Exhaustive checking of a genuinely finite admitted domain can establish a universal claim restricted to that domain with an adequate oracle.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.WHAT_CHANGED_AND_WHAT_DID_NOT: Modern fuzzing, differential oracles and reproducibility improve defect detection/provenance, but their quantified evidence remains distinct from sound universal proofs.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.RESIDUAL_LIMITS: How much empirical confidence a particular corpus provides requires a distribution/risk model not supplied here; no universal numerical confidence estimate is claimed.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.CEREMONY_VERSUS_MECHANISM: Green dashboards, deterministic builds and proof-artifact counts become misleading when their actual proposition and domain are omitted.
CRITICISM_AND_EVOLUTION.RETENTION_RATIONALE: Reject the general evidence-promotion claim while retaining finite testing, provenance and exhaustive finite-domain checking for properly scoped uses.

RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: C0117 retains a predicate-polarity ambiguity after the earlier fixes to C0308/C0309. Its predicate name/plain-language claim asserts the research conclusion that the implication is rejected; its P field combines two strings prefixed Rejected with a different restricted valid inference; its positive witness says there is no positive witness for the rejected universal inference; and the generic verdict rule maps a counterexample to FAIL. Thus the same deterministic-wrong-program witness supports the named research conclusion but is assigned failure under the candidate-universal interpretation. The record does not select one precise proposition for PASS/FAIL.

Two integrated reverse-edge explanations do not describe the reverse of the recorded relation. RM11 goes ordinary compiler correspondence→secure compilation, but its reverse explanation again says ordinary correctness alone does not establish security (the forward insufficiency). RM18 defines a shared finite-testing clause and evidence dependence, which is symmetric on that clause, yet marks every automatic reverse unsupported and explains only why the extra reproducibility clause is not implied by the narrower record. This conflates symmetric partial evidence overlap with directional whole-record implication.

Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

REVIEW_FINDINGS_AND_DISPOSITION.LIMIT: No listed finding is not a guarantee of correctness; reviewers and their sampled documentary checks are described in the validation report.

INTAKE.CROSSWALK_ELIGIBILITY_WITH_REASON: NOT_A_GENERAL_ADOPTION_CANDIDATE: the proposed universal inference is rejected; retain its evidence-domain discriminator and narrower valid alternatives.
TARGET_NEUTRAL_AUDIT_QUESTIONS: Does the claim quantify beyond the tested domain?
Is the receipt about bytes, provenance or semantics?
What complete-domain/oracle argument would justify any universal wording?
PROHIBITED_OVERCLAIMS: Reproducibility proves semantic correctness.
A green finite nonexhaustive conformance suite proves all programs correct.
Testing can never prove anything even in a finite exhaustive domain.
INTAKE.SYNTHESIS_RELEVANT_INTERFACES: EPLT-C0108 distinguishes bounded validation from unbounded proof; EPLT-C0115 distinguishes cache identity/currentness; EPLT-C0116 distinguishes tested residual components from proved correspondence. Root EPLT-C0308 overlaps only the finite-test clause.

A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

CONTRARY_CLAIM_SOURCE_LINKS.LIMIT_OR_OBJECTION: System-author report, not independent randomized productivity study. Generated GADTs/modules/objects have stated limits; effects and library availability remain premises.

HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE.CLAIM: Candidate overclaim admitted from commission's explicit generator/artifact distinction; challenged using historical specialization and modern effectful staging.
HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE.LIMITS: Chronology and conceptual comparison do not establish undocumented historical influence. Universal overclaims are researcher-admitted candidates, not attributed to cited authors.

FORMAL_OR_THEORETICAL_RESULT.CLAIM: Logical refutation of the implication; no empirical defect-rate estimate.
FORMAL_OR_THEORETICAL_RESULT.LIMITS: Constructed counterexamples are analytical witnesses, not reported solver runs. Source theorems retain their own calculus, premises and trust boundaries.

EMPIRICAL_COMPARATIVE_RESULT.CLAIM: MetaOCaml §4.4 gives a well-scoped typed let-insertion example that shares a mutable accumulator across invocations unless a locus prevents motion.
EMPIRICAL_COMPARATIVE_RESULT.LIMITS: Comparisons apply only to the named tasks, versions, baselines, budgets, populations and measures. Sources lacking a comparator cannot establish superiority.

REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.CLAIM: No independent external validation of this complete engineering claim was found in the bounded search.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.LIMITS: Shared data, reference curators, model configurations or opportunistic populations limit independence; absence here is not proof of absence worldwide.

INDUSTRIAL_OR_FIELD_CASE.CLAIM: The effectful code-motion example is a system-level counterexample; no industrial incidence estimate for deterministic-but-wrong generation is provided.
INDUSTRIAL_OR_FIELD_CASE.LIMITS: The analytic non-entailment does not require an incident rate. Do not present the example as an independently observed deployment incident.

NEGATIVE_RESULT_OR_INCIDENT.CLAIM: Constructed decisive counterexample: deterministic g always emits return 0 for intended identity; x=1 separates outcomes. Published reference-allocation motion gives stateful failure.
NEGATIVE_RESULT_OR_INCIDENT.LIMITS: Published failure examples and researcher-constructed counterexamples are explicitly distinguished in the predicate and case records.

STANDARD_OR_NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT.CLAIM: This is an engineering/theoretical or empirical candidate, not an externally mandated requirement.
STANDARD_OR_NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT.LIMITS: A representation standard does not impose a domain policy, create permission, or identify the correct objective.

PRACTITIONER_OR_TOOL_EVIDENCE.CLAIM: Separate reproducibility R(g) from semantic correspondence S(g); compare source and target observations with explicit allocation/effect boundaries.
PRACTITIONER_OR_TOOL_EVIDENCE.LIMITS: Implemented acceptance and system demonstrations do not prove implementation correctness, usability, or universal effectiveness.

TRANSFER_OR_DOMAIN_ANALOGY.CLAIM: Applies to code generators, schemas and deterministic LLM decoding only when someone makes the stronger behavioral inference.
TRANSFER_OR_DOMAIN_ANALOGY.LIMITS: Transfer is an explicit researcher inference; the target population or domain has not been validated merely by conceptual similarity.

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE.CLAIM: Deterministic wrong code is a direct counterexample.
CONTRARY_EVIDENCE.LIMITS: Specification itself may still be wrong even with a correct translation.

ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.CLAIM: Explicit source/target observable behavior and initial state; exact generator/configuration known.
ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.LIMITS: If the requested property really is byte equality, this counterexample addresses a different predicate and is INAPPLICABLE.

SEMANTIC_DEFINITION_ADEQUACY.CLAIM: Universal implication refuted by one generator with R(g)=true and S(g)=false
SEMANTIC_DEFINITION_ADEQUACY.LIMITS: This rejection does not deny the value of reproducible builds or semantics-preserving compilers with actual proofs.

METATHEORETIC_GUARANTEE.CLAIM: No metatheorem is asserted for the empirical generalization or rejected assurance promotion.
METATHEORETIC_GUARANTEE.LIMITS: Logical non-entailment witnesses are not implementation soundness proofs; a model theorem does not prove domain interpretation.

CHECKER_COMPILER_TRUST.CLAIM: Successful staging/type checks do not discharge the effect-order obligation illustrated by mutable-allocation motion.
CHECKER_COMPILER_TRUST.LIMITS: This is a limit on what the checks establish, not evidence that the checker itself is unsound.

IMPLEMENTATION_CORRESPONDENCE.CLAIM: The MetaOCaml system description gives an implemented effectful code-motion example where type/scope acceptance is insufficient for intended behavior.
IMPLEMENTATION_CORRESPONDENCE.LIMITS: The constructed constant-output generator was not executed locally; no general implementation defect rate is claimed.

TRANSFORMATION_COVERAGE.CLAIM: This rejection does not deny the value of reproducible builds or semantics-preserving compilers with actual proofs.
TRANSFORMATION_COVERAGE.LIMITS: No unexamined phase, escape hatch, adapter, foreign call or human interpretation is covered by implication.

EMPIRICAL_USABILITY.CLAIM: MetaOCaml §4.4 gives a well-scoped typed let-insertion example that shares a mutable accumulator across invocations unless a locus prevents motion.
EMPIRICAL_USABILITY.LIMITS: Repairability, test success, compilation and theorem scores are not direct measures of user comprehension or full lifecycle cost.

NATURAL_LANGUAGE_DOMAIN_CORRESPONDENCE.CLAIM: This rejection does not deny the value of reproducible builds or semantics-preserving compilers with actual proofs.
NATURAL_LANGUAGE_DOMAIN_CORRESPONDENCE.LIMITS: Human source/reference adequacy and stakeholder acceptance require separate evidence; no parser, proof or fluent paraphrase supplies them automatically.

EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Counterexample establishes non-entailment only.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.TRANSFERABILITY_LIMITS: Applies to code generators, schemas and deterministic LLM decoding only when someone makes the stronger behavioral inference.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.UNVERIFIED_OR_OPEN_QUESTIONS: Which observations must a concrete generation pipeline preserve?
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.NEXT_DISCRIMINATOR: Add one repeated-call or changed-input test that distinguishes shared state or constant output.

RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.
Eighteen Lane C property lineage fields used the lane label rather than the commissioned lineage ID.

REVIEW_FINDINGS_AND_DISPOSITION.LIMIT: No listed finding is not a guarantee of correctness; reviewers and their sampled documentary checks are described in the validation report.

INTAKE.CROSSWALK_ELIGIBILITY_WITH_REASON: Negative boundary only: do not adopt the universal promotion; use the qualified mechanism and counterexample.
TARGET_NEUTRAL_AUDIT_QUESTIONS: What semantic relation, apart from reproducibility, is asserted?
Could the generator reproduce the same wrong result?
PROHIBITED_OVERCLAIMS: A schema is a correct compiler
A hash proves meaning

STAGING_GENERATION_PROFILE.ALLOWED_EFFECTS: Allocation/effect movement explicitly included in observation.
STAGING_GENERATION_PROFILE.BINDING_TYPE_OBLIGATIONS: Necessary subclaims, insufficient for semantic equivalence.
STAGING_GENERATION_PROFILE.PROVENANCE: Digest identifies artifact; source-to-target mapping explains meaning.

STAGING_GENERATION_PROFILE.LIFECYCLE_COST: Maintain behavioral oracle as templates and targets change.

Lower-cost option already recorded: A dozen stable mapping rows can use a table and small validator; one-off exceptional logic may remain in a host language. Applicability and evidence limit: A table and small validator may be the cheapest adequate option while the stated guard remains true. That comparison can support the proportionate-choice rationale; it does not automatically PASS the precise positive predicate that a custom DSL choice has adequate coverage and benefits exceeding lifecycle cost. HISTORICAL_PROVENANCE.CLAIM: DSL and parser-generator traditions precede modern workbenches;2015 challenge comparison and 2022/2026 user studies make evaluation burdens explicit.

FORMAL_OR_THEORETICAL_RESULT.CLAIM: Contextual decision support; current studies do not establish broad industrial lifecycle return.
FORMAL_OR_THEORETICAL_RESULT.LIMITS: This record appraises empirical decision evidence, not a new formal theorem.

EMPIRICAL_COMPARATIVE_RESULT.CLAIM: Athos shows task/population-specific comparative benefits; workbench challenge demonstrates implementation feature reuse; Neverlang separates comprehension from acceptance.
EMPIRICAL_COMPARATIVE_RESULT.LIMITS: Comparisons apply only to the named tasks, versions, baselines, budgets, populations and measures. Sources lacking a comparator cannot establish superiority.

REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.CLAIM: No independent external validation of this complete engineering claim was found in the bounded search.
REPLICATION_OR_EXTERNAL_VALIDATION.LIMITS: Shared data, reference curators, model configurations or opportunistic populations limit independence; absence here is not proof of absence worldwide.

INDUSTRIAL_OR_FIELD_CASE.CLAIM: The inspected workbench comparison and Athos/Neverlang studies do not provide a controlled industrial lifecycle comparison of a custom DSL against cheaper representations.
INDUSTRIAL_OR_FIELD_CASE.LIMITS: Tool-author implementations and academic cohorts remain useful but cannot establish long-term industrial maintenance benefit.

NEGATIVE_RESULT_OR_INCIDENT.CLAIM: Constructed one-page mapping DSL requires a custom IDE but performs the same checks as a spreadsheet; cost dominates absent measured gain.
NEGATIVE_RESULT_OR_INCIDENT.LIMITS: Published failure examples and researcher-constructed counterexamples are explicitly distinguished in the predicate and case records.

STANDARD_OR_NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT.CLAIM: This is an engineering/theoretical or empirical candidate, not an externally mandated requirement.
STANDARD_OR_NORMATIVE_REQUIREMENT.LIMITS: A representation standard does not impose a domain policy, create permission, or identify the correct objective.

PRACTITIONER_OR_TOOL_EVIDENCE.CLAIM: Compare semantic coverage, invalid-state prevention, escape frequency, diagnostic quality and user effort across DSL, host API, table and checked document.
PRACTITIONER_OR_TOOL_EVIDENCE.LIMITS: Implemented acceptance and system demonstrations do not prove implementation correctness, usability, or universal effectiveness.

TRANSFER_OR_DOMAIN_ANALOGY.CLAIM: Academic routing and workbench reading tasks cannot rank a different industrial domain without new comparators.
TRANSFER_OR_DOMAIN_ANALOGY.LIMITS: Transfer is an explicit researcher inference; the target population or domain has not been validated merely by conceptual similarity.

CONTRARY_EVIDENCE.CLAIM: DSL advocacy often measures tiny demonstrations or code size while omitting learning, migration and exceptional cases.
CONTRARY_EVIDENCE.LIMITS: Longitudinal industrial maintenance and accessibility evidence remain sparse in inspected studies.

ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.CLAIM: Representative tasks/users; cost horizon includes maintenance; semantics and exception demand can be stated; comparison provides comparable training/tool support.
ASSUMPTION_SENSITIVITY.LIMITS: Domain drift drives unvalidated escapes; training favors one option; tool dependencies consume savings.

SEMANTIC_DEFINITION_ADEQUACY.CLAIM: Compare all material alternatives on the same declared task/user/horizon scope; no universal ranking
SEMANTIC_DEFINITION_ADEQUACY.LIMITS: No general DSL superiority; fewer tokens/SLOC alone do not establish fewer errors or lower total cost.

METATHEORETIC_GUARANTEE.CLAIM: No metatheorem is asserted for the empirical generalization or rejected assurance promotion.
METATHEORETIC_GUARANTEE.LIMITS: Logical non-entailment witnesses are not implementation soundness proofs; a model theorem does not prove domain interpretation.

CHECKER_COMPILER_TRUST.CLAIM: The DSL choice predicate concerns domain fit and lifecycle comparison, not a checker or compiler soundness theorem.
CHECKER_COMPILER_TRUST.LIMITS: If a proposed DSL’s benefit depends on a particular checker, that local trust claim must be supplied separately under EPLT-C0204.

IMPLEMENTATION_CORRESPONDENCE.CLAIM: The adoption decision compares representations and costs; it is not itself a formal semantics-to-implementation correspondence claim.
IMPLEMENTATION_CORRESPONDENCE.LIMITS: Specific implementation obligations belong to the chosen language and must be evaluated separately.

TRANSFORMATION_COVERAGE.CLAIM: No general DSL superiority; fewer tokens/SLOC alone do not establish fewer errors or lower total cost.
TRANSFORMATION_COVERAGE.LIMITS: No unexamined phase, escape hatch, adapter, foreign call or human interpretation is covered by implication.

EMPIRICAL_USABILITY.CLAIM: Athos shows task/population-specific comparative benefits; workbench challenge demonstrates implementation feature reuse; Neverlang separates comprehension from acceptance.
EMPIRICAL_USABILITY.LIMITS: Repairability, test success, compilation and theorem scores are not direct measures of user comprehension or full lifecycle cost.

NATURAL_LANGUAGE_DOMAIN_CORRESPONDENCE.CLAIM: No general DSL superiority; fewer tokens/SLOC alone do not establish fewer errors or lower total cost.
NATURAL_LANGUAGE_DOMAIN_CORRESPONDENCE.LIMITS: Human source/reference adequacy and stakeholder acceptance require separate evidence; no parser, proof or fluent paraphrase supplies them automatically.

EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.EVIDENCE_CEILING: Controlled task studies and tool demonstrations, with limited long-term and industry transfer.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.TRANSFERABILITY_LIMITS: Academic routing and workbench reading tasks cannot rank a different industrial domain without new comparators.
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.UNVERIFIED_OR_OPEN_QUESTIONS: Does benefit survive years of domain change, training turnover and unsupported exceptions?
EVIDENCE_AND_UNCERTAINTY.NEXT_DISCRIMINATOR: Run a small matched task/repair comparison and one representative migration; record all excluded tasks.

RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.
Eighteen Lane C property lineage fields used the lane label rather than the commissioned lineage ID.

REVIEW_FINDINGS_AND_DISPOSITION.LIMIT: No listed finding is not a guarantee of correctness; reviewers and their sampled documentary checks are described in the validation report.

INTAKE.CROSSWALK_ELIGIBILITY_WITH_REASON: Eligible as a bounded, target-neutral question or obligation after applicability and local premises are established.
TARGET_NEUTRAL_AUDIT_QUESTIONS: Can an existing host API or table enforce the same critical constraints?
Who owns extension and migration costs?
PROHIBITED_OVERCLAIMS: Shorter notation means lower lifecycle cost
Projectional editing is inherently more usable
A demonstration proves domain-user productivity

LANGUAGE_ENGINEERING_PROFILE.SEMANTIC_SCOPE: Named domain constructs and exceptional cases, not a generic configuration label.

APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Known non-trigger: Only one tool consumes the language and no independently defined language fragments/extensions are combined; for example, a standalone checker has no derived services or fragment composition. Lower-cost option already recorded: A small schema checked by one interpreter needs no workbench; reuse existing parser and schema validator. Applicability and evidence limit: Reusing an existing parser, schema or interpreter can cheaply satisfy an applicable shared-definition/composition obligation if every actual consumer and integration relation is covered. Small tools are not inapplicable merely because no workbench is needed; multiple consumers or combined fragments still trigger A.

APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.SCOPE_AND_EXCLUSIONS: Shared code can share a bug; syntactic composability does not entail semantic preservation or adoption.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.AUTHORITY_OR_NORMATIVE_BASIS_IF_APPLICAB: Researcher’s conditional engineering recommendation, not an external mandate. Where SMT-LIB or LegalRuleML is cited, authority extends to that representation/interface only.

RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: The normalized access-level enum contradicts the actual inspected portions in several records. SB034, SB039 and SB064 are labeled RELEVANT_SECTIONS_INSPECTED although each explicitly records only abstract/metadata access and failed body retrieval. Conversely SA030 is METADATA_ONLY even though its cited 1994 source theorem/definition sections were inspected; only the separately mentioned 1999 version was metadata-only. The aggregate access counts therefore are not counts of the stated source access. The explanatory normalization note does not repair an inaccurate machine value.

Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.
Eighteen Lane C property lineage fields used the lane label rather than the commissioned lineage ID.

REVIEW_FINDINGS_AND_DISPOSITION.LIMIT: No listed finding is not a guarantee of correctness; reviewers and their sampled documentary checks are described in the validation report.

RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: The normalized access-level enum contradicts the actual inspected portions in several records. SB034, SB039 and SB064 are labeled RELEVANT_SECTIONS_INSPECTED although each explicitly records only abstract/metadata access and failed body retrieval. Conversely SA030 is METADATA_ONLY even though its cited 1994 source theorem/definition sections were inspected; only the separately mentioned 1999 version was metadata-only. The aggregate access counts therefore are not counts of the stated source access. The explanatory normalization note does not repair an inaccurate machine value.

Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.
Eighteen Lane C property lineage fields used the lane label rather than the commissioned lineage ID.

REVIEW_FINDINGS_AND_DISPOSITION.LIMIT: No listed finding is not a guarantee of correctness; reviewers and their sampled documentary checks are described in the validation report.

RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: The normalized access-level enum contradicts the actual inspected portions in several records. SB034, SB039 and SB064 are labeled RELEVANT_SECTIONS_INSPECTED although each explicitly records only abstract/metadata access and failed body retrieval. Conversely SA030 is METADATA_ONLY even though its cited 1994 source theorem/definition sections were inspected; only the separately mentioned 1999 version was metadata-only. The aggregate access counts therefore are not counts of the stated source access. The explanatory normalization note does not repair an inaccurate machine value.

Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.
Eighteen Lane C property lineage fields used the lane label rather than the commissioned lineage ID.

REVIEW_FINDINGS_AND_DISPOSITION.LIMIT: No listed finding is not a guarantee of correctness; reviewers and their sampled documentary checks are described in the validation report.

RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: Some evidence partitions reuse claims from another evidence dimension, creating incorrect claim-to-source/partition mappings despite accurate surrounding narrative.

The normalized access-level enum contradicts the actual inspected portions in several records. SB034, SB039 and SB064 are labeled RELEVANT_SECTIONS_INSPECTED although each explicitly records only abstract/metadata access and failed body retrieval. Conversely SA030 is METADATA_ONLY even though its cited 1994 source theorem/definition sections were inspected; only the separately mentioned 1999 version was metadata-only. The aggregate access counts therefore are not counts of the stated source access. The explanatory normalization note does not repair an inaccurate machine value.

Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.
Eighteen Lane C property lineage fields used the lane label rather than the commissioned lineage ID.

REVIEW_FINDINGS_AND_DISPOSITION.LIMIT: No listed finding is not a guarantee of correctness; reviewers and their sampled documentary checks are described in the validation report.

APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: An observational or narrow experimental result is promoted into a general causal defect claim.

Lower-cost option already recorded: For a known type mismatch excluded by a sound checker, use the type guarantee directly without claiming a population-wide defect reduction. Applicability and evidence limit: A sound checker may directly rule out a named mismatch without any population-wide defect claim. That narrow guarantee is a different target. If the causal promotion is advanced, A remains true and the source/causal-identification limits must be assessed; dispute or missing confound evidence is not proof of a zero effect.

RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: Some evidence partitions reuse claims from another evidence dimension, creating incorrect claim-to-source/partition mappings despite accurate surrounding narrative.

Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.
Eighteen Lane C property lineage fields used the lane label rather than the commissioned lineage ID.

Any statistical association establishes causal superiority

Lower-cost option already recorded: For low-risk finite output, a concise direct test or human review may be adequate; full verification cost is claim-dependent. RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.
Eighteen Lane C property lineage fields used the lane label rather than the commissioned lineage ID.

RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: The normalized access-level enum contradicts the actual inspected portions in several records. SB034, SB039 and SB064 are labeled RELEVANT_SECTIONS_INSPECTED although each explicitly records only abstract/metadata access and failed body retrieval. Conversely SA030 is METADATA_ONLY even though its cited 1994 source theorem/definition sections were inspected; only the separately mentioned 1999 version was metadata-only. The aggregate access counts therefore are not counts of the stated source access. The explanatory normalization note does not repair an inaccurate machine value.

Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.
Eighteen Lane C property lineage fields used the lane label rather than the commissioned lineage ID.

REVIEW_FINDINGS_AND_DISPOSITION.LIMIT: No listed finding is not a guarantee of correctness; reviewers and their sampled documentary checks are described in the validation report.

RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: The public-documentation projection presents two preserved rejected candidate propositions as headings under Citation-ready mechanism claims without explicitly stating their rejection in the entries. A non-specialist or downstream writer can take the false headline as the retained result.

The normalized access-level enum contradicts the actual inspected portions in several records. SB034, SB039 and SB064 are labeled RELEVANT_SECTIONS_INSPECTED although each explicitly records only abstract/metadata access and failed body retrieval. Conversely SA030 is METADATA_ONLY even though its cited 1994 source theorem/definition sections were inspected; only the separately mentioned 1999 version was metadata-only. The aggregate access counts therefore are not counts of the stated source access. The explanatory normalization note does not repair an inaccurate machine value.

Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.
Eighteen Lane C property lineage fields used the lane label rather than the commissioned lineage ID.

REVIEW_FINDINGS_AND_DISPOSITION.LIMIT: No listed finding is not a guarantee of correctness; reviewers and their sampled documentary checks are described in the validation report.

RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.
Eighteen Lane C property lineage fields used the lane label rather than the commissioned lineage ID.

RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.
Eighteen Lane C property lineage fields used the lane label rather than the commissioned lineage ID.

APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Two or more components interpret the same externally supplied input for a consequential decision.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Known non-trigger: Fewer than two components interpret the same externally supplied input for a consequential decision; for example, a table is displayed once with no downstream automated interpretation or cross-consumer agreement claim. Lower-cost option already recorded: A single parser with one immutable parsed value and no reinterpretation may need only a documented format contract. Applicability and evidence limit: One parser and an immutable parsed value can reduce duplicate interpretation. If two consumers still derive consequential interpretations from that value, A remains true and a shared decision projection can cheaply establish their agreement. Shared parsing alone is not proof that every consumer interprets the value identically.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ASSUMPTIONS_AND_PRECONDITIONS: The relevant consumers and interpretation projection are complete; same input bytes/version reach both; no unmodeled later coercion.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ENVIRONMENT_AND_BOUNDARY: Agreement concerns selected fields and meanings, not byte equality or complete application authorization.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.SCOPE_AND_EXCLUSIONS: Conditional semantic agreement within inventoried boundary; no global security or external-intent guarantee.

DEPENDENCIES_AND_CONFLICTS.premises: The relevant consumers and interpretation projection are complete; same input bytes/version reach both; no unmodeled later coercion.
DEPENDENCIES_AND_CONFLICTS.tensions: Sharing a parser alone does not prove consumers agree after coercion, defaults or interpretation.

APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.RETIREMENT_OR_REENTRY_CONDITION: Retire the extra mechanism when its trigger disappears and no consumer depends on it; re-enter when two or more components interpret the same externally supplied input for a consequential decision.
