RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.ENGINEERING_CLAIM: A review environment should expose language-relevant structure and suspicious confusables according to a declared Unicode/language policy.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.BEARER_OR_SUBJECT: Human code reviewer, editor, diff viewer and compiler diagnostic reader.

CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.MATURE_OR_EVOLVED_FORM: Current Unicode guidance treats lexical structure and multilingual usability as joint constraints; this is narrower than a universal character-ban prescription.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.EXPECTED_PAYOFF: Makes specified display-versus-token discrepancies inspectable without treating non-Latin text as inherently invalid.
CLAIM_AND_MECHANISM.PAYOFF_EVIDENCE_NOT_JUST_RATIONALE: Boucher/Anderson §3 supplies working mechanisms; UTS55 §§1.2,4.1,5.2 supplies counterexamples and conditional handling requirements.

APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.TRIGGER_OR_CONTEXT: Human review or debugging of Unicode source in an environment whose display can differ from lexical structure.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.NON_TRIGGER_OR_CHEAP_PATH: Known non-trigger: There is no human review/debugging of Unicode source in an environment whose display can differ from lexical structure; for example, processing is machine-only with no human-presentation claim. Lower-cost option already recorded: For a justified ASCII-only language/domain, enforce the small declared alphabet and still check line endings and interpretation. Applicability and evidence limit: A justified restricted alphabet and simple display checks may cheaply satisfy the scoped presentation requirement. Alphabet restriction is not automatically a false guard while human review and relevant display/lexical differences remain. Byte interpretation remains a separate obligation.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ASSUMPTIONS_AND_PRECONDITIONS: Correct lexical segmentation for the language and Unicode version; diagnostics are visible; nested embedded languages have an explicit policy.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.ENVIRONMENT_AND_BOUNDARY: Readability and spoofing exposure; does not establish a program’s intended function or reviewer comprehension.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.SCOPE_AND_EXCLUSIONS: Specified rendering/conformance behavior plus demonstrated attacks; comparative real-world review benefit remains unmeasured here.
APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.AUTHORITY_OR_NORMATIVE_BASIS_IF_APPLICAB: No target authority or adoption follows. RFC/UTS clauses apply only to their expressly claimed conformance scope.

APPLICABILITY_AND_AUTHORITY.RETIREMENT_OR_REENTRY_CONDITION: Retire the extra mechanism when its trigger disappears and no consumer depends on it; re-enter when human review or debugging of unicode source in an environment whose display can differ from lexical structure.

RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: The normalized access-level enum contradicts the actual inspected portions in several records. SB034, SB039 and SB064 are labeled RELEVANT_SECTIONS_INSPECTED although each explicitly records only abstract/metadata access and failed body retrieval. Conversely SA030 is METADATA_ONLY even though its cited 1994 source theorem/definition sections were inspected; only the separately mentioned 1999 version was metadata-only. The aggregate access counts therefore are not counts of the stated source access. The explanatory normalization note does not repair an inaccurate machine value.

Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

records.title: Blanket directional-character bans as complete spoofing prevention

IDENTITY.PROPERTY_NAME: Blanket directional-character bans as complete spoofing prevention

GENEALOGY.HISTORICAL_ORIGIN: Analytical overgeneralization of a simple mitigation discussed in Trojan Source; compared with UTS55 counterexamples and multilingual requirements.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_TERMINOLOGY: Character banning; modern gloss: mistaking one attack filter for complete representation security.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_FORM: The proposed filter removes one class of code points; it does not examine lexical display, confusable identifiers or control-free ambiguities.
GENEALOGY.ORIGINAL_PROBLEM: A cheap filter is treated as a sufficient solution for all human/compiler disagreement.

RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: Two integrated reverse-edge explanations do not describe the reverse of the recorded relation. RM11 goes ordinary compiler correspondence→secure compilation, but its reverse explanation again says ordinary correctness alone does not establish security (the forward insufficiency). RM18 defines a shared finite-testing clause and evidence dependence, which is symmetric on that clause, yet marks every automatic reverse unsupported and explains only why the extra reproducibility clause is not implied by the narrower record. This conflates symmetric partial evidence overlap with directional whole-record implication.

Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.

RELEVANT_FINDINGS.FINDING: Several fields named INAPPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS contain only a cheaper sufficient method, although the record’s applicability guard remains true. A known source/target identity pair still meets C0108’s need for a checked preservation relation; direct equality can satisfy it cheaply. A finite straight-line computation whose completion is required still meets C0113’s eventuality/termination guard; bounded evaluation may prove it without fairness machinery. A small interpreter still falls under C0116 if the assurance claim concerns the executing runtime. Mapping these conditions to INAPPLICABLE conflicts with the declared A/P/E rule that only a known false guard yields that outcome, and can erase an applicable obligation precisely because it already has a proportionate mechanism.
